item.title: Foata and Spot Commutation for Parking Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a parking function $\alpha$, let $\mathrm{spot}(\alpha)$ be the permutation whose $i$th entry is the space occupied by car $i$ and let $\mathrm{foata}(w)$ be Foata's second fundamental transformation on words. Conjecture 6.3 of Celano et al. asserts that $\mathrm{foata}(\mathrm{spot}(\alpha)) = \mathrm{spot}(\mathrm{foata}(\alpha))$ for every unit interval parking function $\alpha$. This paper proves the identity for a larger class: parking functions where each prime component (borrowing Gessel's definition) of $\alpha$ is nondecreasing. Since every unit interval parking function is composed of nondecreasing prime parking functions, the conjecture follows. A key step is showing that $\mathrm{foata}$ preserves the set of parking functions $\alpha$ with $\mathrm{spot}(\alpha) = \mathrm{std}(\alpha)$, where $\mathrm{std}$ denotes standardization. In particular, this proves that inversion count and major index are equidistributed over this larger class.
item.dc:creator: Eshaan Sombhatta

item.title: Forsyth--Glaisher-Type Series for $1/\pi$ Involving Catalan Numbers and Harmonic Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.28059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an elementary method for constructing and evaluating families of Forsyth--Glaisher-type series for $1/\pi$. The approach is based on Newton's generalized binomial theorem, identities for generalized binomial coefficients, and Euler's beta integral, together with properties of the gamma and digamma functions. We establish several parameterized identities involving squares of central binomial coefficients and products of odd integers, from which we derive explicit evaluations in terms of $1/\pi$. By means of transformations connecting generalized binomial coefficients with Catalan numbers, we obtain further families of series involving squares of Catalan numbers. We also derive identities for series involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers by differentiating suitable parameter-dependent formulas. These results yield evaluations containing both $1/\pi$ and logarithmic terms, particularly $\ln 2$. Our results provide a unified framework for generating and evaluating related binomial and Catalan-type series and reveal connections among central binomial coefficients, Catalan numbers, and harmonic numbers.
item.dc:creator: Kunle Adegoke, Robert Frontczak, Taras Goy

item.title: Short Paper No. 2: Relations between integer sequences A003622 $\&$ A035336 and two criteria in respect of maximum degrees within the family of finite linear Jaco graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.28060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes two relationships between integer sequences and the maximum degrees of finite linear Jaco graphs $J_n(x)$. First, it characterizes the positive maximum degrees that occur exactly once within the family, showing that they are generated by the integer sequence A003622. Second, it determines the orders of the corresponding graphs and establishes their relationship with the integer sequence A035336. These results resolve conjectures previously stated in [5]. The proofs were developed with the assistance of AI-based mathematical reasoning technology and subsequently reviewed by the authors.
item.dc:creator: Timoth\'ee Raso, Johan Kok

item.title: The Rotation Strategy Wins Penney's game for Permutations
item.description: arXiv:2611.28063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Penney's game for permutations, two players choose distinct patterns of the same length $k$, and independent random variables with a common continuous distribution are observed until the relative order of $k$ consecutive observations matches one of the patterns; the player who chose that pattern wins. Elizalde and Lin conjectured that the second player wins with probability greater than one half by answering the pattern $a_1a_2\cdots a_k$ with its rotation $a_ka_1\cdots a_{k-1}$. We prove that this conjecture holds for every $k\ge3$. We also show that for $k\ge8$ the rotation wins with probability at least $1/2+0.0053/(k+1)$. The proof writes the advantage of the second player in terms of clusters, which are chains of overlapping marked occurrences of the two patterns weighted by $\pm1$. We show that, for each ordering of the observations, the weights of its clusters sum to $-1$, $0$, or $1$. This gives an explicit bound on the contribution of arbitrarily long clusters, which proves the result analytically for $k\ge8$, and exact rational computations prove it for $3\le k\le7$.
item.dc:creator: Himaghna Roy Choudhury

item.title: Combinatorial Zeta Functions of Type $\widetilde A_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.28064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a combinatorial zeta theory for finite colored triangular complexes $X$ whose vertex links satisfy a local hexagon condition. Their edge and chamber zeta functions $Z_1(X,u)$ and $Z_2(X,u)$ are Euler products over primitive closed geodesics. The M\"obius functions of the augmented local incidence posets define a vertex polynomial $M(X,u)$. We prove the identity $\frac{Z_1(X,u)}{Z_2(X,-u)} = (1-u^3)^{\chi(X)}M(X,u)^{-1}$, where $\chi(X)$ is the Euler characteristic of $X$. The proof reconstructs the cohomological operator framework for finite $\mathrm{PGL}_3$ quotients from the local link data: the degree operators recover the three determinant factors and together form a cochain map homotopic to multiplication by $1-u^3$. Sylvester's identity gives the resulting alternating determinant relation directly. All constructions use only the finite incidence structure of $X$; no ambient group, field, or building is required.
item.dc:creator: Ming-Hsuan Kang, Chian-Jen Wang

item.title: Quadratic periods and preperiods in subtraction games with one varying move
item.description: arXiv:2611.28065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give two infinite families of counterexamples to Zhang's conjectures on the period and preperiod of the Sprague-Grundy sequence when a single move c is adjoined to a fixed subtraction set S. For S = {4,5,10} and c = 15t+13 with t >= 2, the least period is c+19 and the least preperiod is (c^2+21c+8)/15. For S = {3,7,10} and c = 90t+9 with t >= 1, the least period is (c^2+26c+615)/30 and the least preperiod is 19 less than the period. The latter quadratic period also occurs in the outcome sequence, which is periodic from its first term. The proofs construct the sequences from fixed words and reduce the mex recurrence to a finite table of local identities.
item.dc:creator: Ruiqi Zhao, Qi Zhang, Zhihao Shi

item.title: Face-neighbourly polyhedra with eight or nine faces and genus at most three
item.description: arXiv:2611.28066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A polyhedral surface is face-neighbourly if every pair of faces shares an edge. We classify the combinatorial types of closed orientable face-neighbourly polyhedral surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with eight or nine faces and genus at most three, assuming trivalent vertices, simple planar polygonal faces and distinct supporting planes for adjacent faces. Several common edges between a pair of faces are allowed. The enumeration gives 42,124 candidate maps with eight faces and 203 with nine. SAT certificates exclude all but two maps, both of genus three with eight nonagonal faces. They are realised by Mizhaev's V2 and by the R\"ost--V\'igh polyhedron. With the face-neighbourliness condition removed, the class of genus-three surfaces with eight nonagonal faces has one additional realisable type, Mizhaev's V1.
item.dc:creator: Ruslan Mizhaev

item.title: Externally supported independence in split and proper interval graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.28073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An independent set $B$ in a graph $G=(V,E)$ satisfying the additional condition that the vertices in $N(B)$ are dominated by vertices in $V(G) \setminus N[B]$ is called an externally supported independent set (ESI-set for short). The maximum cardinality of such a set in $G$ is called externally supported independence number of $G$. We study the externally supported independence number in split graphs and proper interval graphs, two graph classes with unbounded clique-width. For split graphs we investigate the structure and computational complexity of the ESI Set problem. We prove that the ESI Set problem remains NP-complete when restricted to split graphs, while also establishing simple upper and lower bounds for the externally supported independence number. These bounds are sharp for a wide range of split graphs. For split graphs, we further investigate the relationship between the externally supported independence number and the isolation number. In particular, we characterize when an optimal ESI-set yields an optimal isolating set, and conversely, when an optimal isolating set yields an optimal ESI-set. Finally, we consider proper interval graphs and present a linear-time algorithm for finding a maximum ESI-set of an arbitrary proper interval graph.
item.dc:creator: Dragana Bo\v{z}ovi\'c, Tanja Dravec, Aleksander Kelenc

item.title: Enumerative Chromatic Choosability of Complete Multipartite Graphs with Small Partite Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.28340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chromatic choosability is a notion of fundamental importance in list coloring. A graph is chromatic-choosable when its chromatic number is equal to its list chromatic number. In their 1979 paper on list coloring, Erd\H{o}s, Rubin, and Taylor showed that complete $m$-partite graphs with every partite set of size 2, denoted by $K_{2*m}$, are chromatic-choosable. In 1990, Kostochka and Sidorenko introduced the list color function of a graph $G$, denoted by $P_{\ell}(G,m)$, which is the list analogue of the chromatic polynomial of $G$, $P(G,m)$. A graph $G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable when $P_{\ell}(G,m) = P(G,m)$ whenever $m \in \mathbb{N}$. In this paper, we explore the question as to whether $K_{2*m}$ satisfies this stronger property. We establish a recursive lower bound on $P_{\ell}(K_{2*m},m)$ and prove that $K_{2*3}$ and $K_{2*4}$ are weakly enumeratively chromatic-choosable, meaning that equality holds at the chromatic number. We also develop a general lower bound for the list color function of certain joins with complete graphs and use it to prove that $K_p\vee K_{2*5}$ is weakly enumeratively chromatic-choosable whenever $p\geq 15$, and that $K_p\vee K_{2,2,3}$ is weakly enumeratively chromatic-choosable whenever $p\geq 3$. These results provide progress toward a weaker form of a conjecture of Allred and Mudrock concerning the enumerative chromatic choosability of complete graph joins.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Allred, Joseph T. Brown, Devin Dickinson, H. C. Fritz, Aiden McCain, Jeffrey A. Mudrock, Daniel Smith, Morgan Taylor, Benjamin Whatley

item.title: Triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes
item.description: arXiv:2611.28360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fractional triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes, unifying the settings of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions and the high-dimensional Dirac problem for Steiner triple systems. We prove that every sufficiently large two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum degree at least $(1-d_1)n$ and maximum missing codegree at most $d_2n$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition, provided $d_1/0.21+d_2/0.27\leq 1$. As an immediate consequence, we prove the asymptotic form of Lee's high-dimensional Dirac conjecture: every sufficiently large admissible $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum codegree at least $(3/4+\varepsilon)n$ contains a Steiner triple system. We also provide constructions establishing lower bounds on this fractional decomposition threshold problem.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Delcourt, Thomas Lesgourgues, Luke Postle

item.title: Failed Vertex Covering Graph Reconfiguration
item.description: arXiv:2611.28406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A failed vertex cover of a graph is a vertex set that leaves at least one edge uncovered. The associated token addition and removal (TAR) graph has the failed vertex covers as vertices, with two sets adjacent when they differ by one vertex. We characterize when two finite graphs have isomorphic failed vertex cover TAR graphs, allowing disconnected graphs, loops, and parallel edges.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Hall, Rogelio Tovar

item.title: A general triangle generation of the $d$-dimensional Genocchi numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.28407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a uniform recurrence relation for the rook numbers of generalized Genocchi boards of dimension $d\geq 3$. The recurrence for each row of the rook-number triangle is expressed in terms of the preceding row, with coefficients given by products of consecutive powers and finite sums involving Stirling numbers of the second kind. The proof decomposes the boundary of the board into blocks that correspond to the coordinates equal to 1. A coordinatewise counting argument then shows that the number of extensions of a fixed interior placement depends on a boundary partition only through the number of its blocks and the size of their union. We also express the coefficients as finite differences, recovering the previously established recurrences in dimensions three through five, and give the six-dimensional specialization. As a complementary result, we formulate an injection model that provides a direct bijective proof of a formerly established identification of the diagonal rook numbers with generalized Genocchi numbers.
item.dc:creator: Derek Hanely, Edison Mu\c{c}llari, Vasily Zadorozhnyy

item.title: Essential and disjoint edge numbers for graphs and hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.28415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the extension to arbitrary forbidden sets of the property that every graph has a bipartition over which at least half of the graph edges are cross-edges, and obtain analogous results in the hypergraph setting.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Karam

item.title: A characterization of Ramsey property with application to dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.28425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The infinitary Ramsey theorem says that in any finite partition {V^i;~i=1,2,\cdots,n} of the the family of k-subsets of N, there exists V^i having an infinite subset M of N such that any k-set from M is in V^i. This property of V^i is called the Ramsey property. We characterize this property in term of ultrafilter.
item.dc:creator: Teturo Kamae

item.title: Totally odd clique immersions in graphs with bounded independence number
item.description: arXiv:2611.28470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every $n$-vertex graph with at least one edge and independence number at most an integer $a\ge2$, where $n\ge a$, contains a totally odd strong immersion of \[ K_{\left\lceil (n+a-1)/(2a-3/2) \right\rceil}, \] with every branch path of length at most $2a-1$. We also prove that every graph $G$ with independence number at most $a$ and no totally odd strong $K_t$-immersion with branch paths of length at most $2a-1$ satisfies \[ \chi(G)\le\left\lfloor \frac{(2a-3/2)(t-1)-a+2}{2} \right\rfloor \] where $t\ge2$. These bounds reduce the leading denominator coefficient in the general order bound from $9/4$ to $2$ and the colouring coefficient for independence number two from $3/2$ to $5/4$.
item.dc:creator: Sebasti\'an Bustamante

item.title: From two heptagrams to a 449-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.28518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a 5-chromatic unit-distance graph on 449 vertices. Previously, the smallest known 5-chromatic unit-distance graph had 509 vertices. Our graph is a subgraph of a graph obtained by a simple greedy construction applied to a 14-vertex seed graph consisting of two heptagrams.
item.dc:creator: Marijn J. H. Heule, Benjamin Przybocki

item.title: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
item.description: arXiv:2611.28580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An integral matrix $A$ has the Edmonds-Johnson property if, for all integral vectors $b,c,l,u$, the first Chv\'atal closure of $\{x: b\le Ax\le c,\ l\le x\le u\}$ equals its integer hull. Gerards and Schrijver conjectured that a totally half-modular matrix has the Edmonds-Johnson property if and only if it has no minor equal to one of two specific matrices, of size $3\times3$ and $3\times4$. We disprove this conjecture. We give a totally half-modular $5\times6$ matrix that does not have the Edmonds-Johnson property and has no minor equal to either matrix. It is a minimal obstruction: every proper minor has the Edmonds-Johnson property. The proofs work on a graph whose edges are the rows and bounds of the matrix, and on which the minor operations act by deleting, contracting and halving edges. For minimality, we reduce every proper minor to two classes of matrices known to have the Edmonds-Johnson property.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Del Pia

item.title: Spectral radii of connected graphs with prescribed maximum degree
item.description: arXiv:2611.28588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a real number $\alpha>0$ and a positive integer $r$, we give recursive characterizations of the existence of finite simple connected graphs $G$ with adjacency spectral radius $\rho(G)=\alpha$ and maximum degree $\Delta(G)\le r$ (or $=r$). Adding one vertex to a graph $F$ at a time to update the Schur-complement $q=\alpha-{\mathbf b}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}{\mathbf b}$, where $B=\alpha I-A(F)$ is positive definite and ${\mathbf b}$ is a nonzero $0$--$1$ that specifies the neighbours of $z$ in $F$. Realizability is characterized by admissible constructions with positive intermediate outputs $q$ and a final zero output. We also establish a reduction for a graph $G$ obtained by attaching pairwise disjoint rooted trees, each by a single edge, to a nonempty connected graph $H$. Assume that $\alpha I-A(T)\succ0$ for every attached tree $T$. For each $z\in V(H)$, let $q_{z,1},\ldots,q_{z,s_z}$ be the positive root pivots obtained by the scalar tree recursion for the trees attached to $z$, and set \[ a_z=\alpha-\sum_{j=1}^{s_z}q_{z,j}^{-1}, \qquad M_H(\mathbf a)=\operatorname{diag}(a_z:z\in V(H))-A(H), \] where an empty sum is zero. Then $\rho(G)=\alpha$ if and only if $M_H(\mathbf a)\succeq0$ and $\det M_H(\mathbf a)=0$. Taking $H=K_1$ recovers the tree criteria, while $\delta(H)\geq2$ gives criteria for graphs with prescribed 2-core $H$. In particular, for unicyclic graphs of prescribed cycle length, path continuants reduce the spectral condition to positivity inequalities and one scalar equation.
item.dc:creator: Fengming Dong

item.title: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.28619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The principal ideal of a composition consists of its distinct generalized subwords, ranked by the sum of their parts. We prove rank-unimodality for every composition with at most one descent and for every bitonic composition. Both the part sizes and the number of parts are unrestricted. The main ingredient is a coupling for a monotone host. If a subword is chosen uniformly among those of weight at most n, its length and its unused weight can be made to increase weakly when n increases by one. A decreasing threshold on the next available part then compares the positive difference of two ordinary rank coefficients with an earlier cumulative ratio. This supplies the coefficient inequality in the hereditary reduction at a strict peak.
item.dc:creator: Yibo Zhang, Zhanhe Zhang

item.title: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
item.description: arXiv:2611.28659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$. We show that the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, $n\geq2$, is a $2$-Cayley regression if and only if it is a $3$-Cayley regression, which holds exactly when $n$ is a prime power, and that for $k\geq4$ it is a $k$-Cayley regression if and only if $n$ is an odd prime power or $n\in\{2,4\}$. Groups with a cyclic subgroup of index two that are neither cyclic nor dihedral are not even $2$-Cayley regressions; consequently, a group with a cyclic subgroup of index two is a Cayley regression if and only if it is isomorphic to $C_2$, $C_4$, $C_6$, $C_{10}$, or $D_{2n}$ with $n$ as above. Finally, every split metacyclic group $C_m\rtimes C_q$ with $m>2$ and odd $q\geq3$ is not a $2$-Cayley regression.
item.dc:creator: Yingbi Jiang, Pengfei Guo, Jin-Hua Xie

item.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
item.description: arXiv:2611.28664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$.
item.dc:creator: D\"om\"ot\"or P\'alv\"olgyi

item.title: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.28672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic. Our results extend the previously known spectral formulas for this family of graphs. We also obtain all the eigenvalues when the characteristic of $R$ is $2$. Furthermore, for rings of odd characteristic, we give a complete characterization of when $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ is a strongly regular Cayley graph.
item.dc:creator: Priya Dhankhar, Sanjay Kumar Singh

item.title: On non-canonical maximum cliques in the block graphs of orthogonal arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.28703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we prove an Erd\H{o}s-Ko-Rado characterisation of maximum intersecting families of columns of certain orthogonal arrays. This solves a problem of Chris Godsil and Karen Meagher and implies that, in all orthogonal arrays OA$(m,(m-1)^2)$, every non-canonical maximum intersecting family of columns necessarily has the structure of an affine plane.
item.dc:creator: Tao Feng, Sergey Goryainov, Elena V. Konstantinova, Letian Zhang

item.title: The inverse Erd\H{o}s--Fuchs problem for $k$-fold sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.28733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every fixed integer $k\ge 3$, we construct an infinite set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{h\le n}r_{kA}(h)=\Gamma(1+1/k)^k n+O_k(n^{(1-1/k)^2})$, where $r_{kA}(h)$ counts ordered representations of $h$ as a sum of $k$ elements of $A$, with repetitions allowed. This improves Dai and Pan's bound for a linear main term. In the paired random model used here, fluctuations of the stated order occur infinitely often almost surely.
item.dc:creator: Aimin Guo, Xiaohui Yan

item.title: Three almost symmetric metatiles generate the Spectre tiling
item.description: arXiv:2611.28888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a system of three `metatiles' for the Spectre aperiodic monotiling, named `D23'. These are similar in concept to the {\HTPF} system for the hat tiling: the metatiles have their own substitution system which can be iterated as many times as desired, and then the lowest-order metatiles can be converted into Spectre tiles. One of the three metatiles has order-2 rotational symmetry, and the other two are `almost symmetric' with orders 2 and 3 respectively, in the sense that although the region covered by the tile's $n$-times deflation is not exactly identical to its rotation, within their intersection, the proportion of non-matching tiles tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$. This near-symmetry corresponds to cases of near-symmetry in the Spectre tiling itself. A curious property of this system is that one of the three metatiles disappears completely in the conversion to Spectres!
item.dc:creator: Simon Tatham

item.title: Independent and end-faithful spanning trees in infinite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.28938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spanning trees rooted at the same vertex are independent if, for each vertex other than the root, the paths from the root to that vertex are pairwise distinct and internally vertex-disjoint. Zehavi and Itai conjectured that, for every positive integer $k$, every finite $k$-connected graph has $k$ independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. We show that every $2$-connected graph, finite or infinite, has two independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. For locally finite $2$-connected graphs, both trees can be chosen end-faithful. We also prove that every locally finite $3$-connected chordal graph has three independent end-faithful spanning trees. Counterexamples show that local finiteness is essential for the version with independent end-faithful spanning trees. We further show that every $3$-connected graph with a universal vertex or a finite vertex cover has three independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Santos Monteiro

item.title: Nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in {-1,0,1}
item.description: arXiv:2611.28952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine all nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$. The problem reduces to describing the set $\cN_n$ of pairs $(d,b)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\times\{-1,1\}^{n-1}$ for which the tridiagonal matrices with diagonal $d$ and with products $b_k$ of opposite off-diagonal entries have characteristic polynomial $\lambda^n$. We show that $\cN_n$ is obtained from $\cN_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ by one of two explicit ``folding'' operations, according to the parity of $n$. As a consequence, $\cN_n$ is non-empty precisely when $n=1$ or $3\cdot2^j-1\le n\le2^{j+2}-1$ for some $j\ge0$, in which case it has $2^{\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ elements. This yields a formula for the number of nilpotent $n\times n$ tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, which begins $1,9,73,585,4809,39113$. The case $d=0$ is a conjecture of Corless, established in an earlier paper. The main new ingredient is a rigidity phenomenon: a pair as above, of size $n\ge2$, whose characteristic polynomial is congruent to $\lambda^n$ modulo $4$ is necessarily a fold of a smaller pair. It follows that such a pair is nilpotent as soon as its characteristic polynomial is congruent to $\lambda^n$ modulo $2^{1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$. Finally we show that the eigenvalue zero of an $m\times m$ matrix in Corless's skew-symmetric family has multiplicity at most $2^{v_2(m+1)}-1$, with equality attained. The classification, the rigidity statement, the cardinality of the sets $\cN_n$ and the criterion modulo $2^{1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ have been formalised in Lean~4.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Blattner

item.title: When do local bounds permit optimal edge-colorings?
item.description: arXiv:2611.29111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a multigraph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, maximum multiplicity $\mu(G)$, and chromatic index $\chi'(G)$. A proper edge-coloring is locally bounded if each edge $e$ in $G$ with endvertices $u$ and $v$ is assigned a color at most $\max\{d_G(u)+\mu_G(u),d_G(v)+\mu_G(v)\}$, where $d_G(w)$ and $\mu_G(w)$ respectively denote the degree of $w$ and the maximum multiplicity of an edge incident with $w$. The well-known Vizing's theorem guarantees a proper edge-coloring with at most $\Delta(G)+\mu(G)$ colors. Recently, the local version of this theorem was established for simple graphs by Christiansen, resolving a conjecture posed by Bonamy, Delcourt, Lang, and Postle, and extended to multigraphs by Conley, Greb\'ik, and Pikhurko. In this paper, we define the local chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $\chi'_{loc}(G)$, as the least positive integer $k$ for which $G$ admits a locally bounded proper edge-coloring with colors in $\{1,2,...,k\}$. Thus $\Delta(G)\le\chi'(G)\le\chi'_{loc}(G)\le\Delta(G)+\mu(G)$. We give equivalent characterizations and sufficient conditions for the equality $\chi'_{loc}(G)=\chi'(G)$, identifying when the local bounds in Vizing's theorem can be satisfied using the minimum possible number of colors. In particular, we prove this equality for every regular multigraph, every multigraph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\le 4$, and every simple graph in which the vertices of degree at least five induce a subgraph of maximum degree at most two. Moreover, we construct a simple graph $G$ with $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)=5$ and $\chi'_{loc}(G)=6$, showing that these local bounds can force the use of an additional color even in simple graphs. Consequently, five is the smallest possible maximum degree for which satisfying these local bounds can require more than $\chi'(G)$ colors.
item.dc:creator: Xuli Qi, Minli Yu

item.title: On the General Position Number of Cacti
item.description: arXiv:2611.29136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a graph G=(V,E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges, a subset of vertices $S \subseteq V$ is called a General Position Set (GPS) if no shortest path on G between any two vertices in S contains another vertex from S. The General Position Number (GPN) of a graph G is the maximum size of a GPS in G. The decision version of this problem, determining whether the GPN of a graph G is at least a given integer i, is known as the General Position Problem (GPP). The GPP is known to be NP-complete, making the computation of the GPN for general graphs computationally challenging. Hence, much of the existing research has focused on determining the GPN for special classes of graphs. One such class is that of cactus graphs (i.e., cacti), in which any two simple cycles share at most one vertex and no edge. For cactus graphs, several upper and lower bounds on the GPN have been previously presented. In this paper, we determine the exact value of the GPN for cactus graphs. We propose a novel graph decomposition that partitions a cactus graph into two types of subgraphs, called bearded cycles and non-beard trees. For each subgraph, we compute a special GPS, named a subGPS. We prove that the union of all maximum subGPSs constitutes a maximum GPS for the original cactus graph. This result allows us to compute the exact GPN for any cactus graph.
item.dc:creator: Toshihiko Kimura, Yonghwan Kim, Yoshiaki Katayama

item.title: Rough structure. I. Exclusion among series-parallel graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.29161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is the first in a series of papers about rough structure theorems: graph properties that are implied by the exclusion of some graph as a minor, and imply the exclusion of some larger graph of the same type. Here we look at the structure of the series-parallel graphs that do not contain a given series-parallel graph as a minor. We prove that for every series-parallel graph $H$, there exists $m$ such that every simple two-connected series-parallel graph that does not contain $H$ as a minor admits a tree-decomposition of height at most $m$, where each "torso" is either an outerplanar graph or a planar dual of one. We prove similar theorems about the series-parallel graphs that exclude an outerplanar graph, the series-parallel graphs that exclude a dual of an outerplanar graph, the graphs of tree-width three that exclude a series-parallel graph, and the general graphs that exclude a fan.
item.dc:creator: Maria Chudnovsky, Julien Codsi, Alex Divoux, Paul Seymour, Liana Yepremyan

item.title: Improved Lower Bound on the Hadwiger-Debrunner Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.29166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The celebrated $(p,q)$-theorem of Alon and Kleitman asserts that for any $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and any $p \geq q \geq d+1$, every family of convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ in which among any $p$ sets, some $q$ intersect, can be pierced by $c(p,q,d)$ points. The minimum numbers $c(p,q,d)$ are called the Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers and denoted $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,q)$ and determining them is a longstanding open problem. We prove that for any $d \geq 2$, $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,d+1) \geq p^{d-o(1)}$, and more generally, $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,q) \geq p^{\frac{q-1}{q-d}-o(1)}$. Our bound is obtained by a family of parallelotopes, and is tight up to polylogarithmic factors among all families that have a bounded VC dimension. The proof uses the hypergraph container method.
item.dc:creator: Chaya Keller

item.title: Bruhat Shellings of the Quasisymmetric Flag Moment Complex
item.description: arXiv:2611.29192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quasisymmetric flag variety gives rise to a regular cell complex whose maximal cells are cubes indexed by fully supported noncrossing partitions. Two maximal cubes can meet along several faces. We describe each cube using the block arcs and parent connectors of its indexing partition, and determine its intersection with the union of the preceding cubes in Bruhat order. For each nonempty face, we determine the first maximal cube containing it by applying an outer-block merging operation to its Bruhat-maximal noncrossing-partition label. The first-carrier theorem provides an explicit description of how each cube attaches to the preceding subcomplex. More precisely, the intersection is a union of coordinate facets which, for every cube except the first, forms the closed star of a face in its boundary. Consequently, every linear extension of Bruhat order on the maximal-cell labels gives a shelling of the regular cell complex. In particular, its barycentric subdivision is shellable, hence homotopy Cohen--Macaulay and Cohen--Macaulay over \(\mathbb Z\) and every field.
item.dc:creator: Saffana Khan, Nantel Bergeron

item.title: Quaternary games with infinite mis\`ere quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.29198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the four wild quaternary games left open by the earlier work of Plambeck and Siegel. For \texttt{0.3102} we discover a special regularity of its two--heap case, give a complete solution of the two--heap case, and deduce from it that its mis\`ere quotient is infinite. For \texttt{0.3122} and \texttt{0.3123} we rigorously prove, by slice--wise algebraic periodicity and hierarchical induction (computer--assisted), that their mis\`ere quotients are infinite. For \texttt{0.3312}, as well as many other wild quaternary games, we carry out computations and observations.
item.dc:creator: Kai Liang

item.title: Contiguous relations for elliptic analogues of partial sums of very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series
item.description: arXiv:2611.29300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce finite elliptic analogues of partial sums of a balanced very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series. By combining Abel's lemma on summation by parts with the Riemann theta relation, we establish two contiguous relations. Iterating the second relation gives two finite transformation formulas.
item.dc:creator: Takumi Maesaka

item.title: Optimal odd unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$ through $59$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that the largest minimum norm among unimodular lattices is $4$ in dimension $49$ and $5$ in dimensions $50$, $51$, $57$ and $58$. We also study the theta series of optimal unimodular lattices in every dimension from $49$ through $59$. In dimensions $50$, $51$ and $57$, the first known examples of unimodular lattices with minimum norm $5$ are obtained from self-dual codes by Construction~A. There exist at least $25$, $2$, $3$, $7$ and $12$ nonisomorphic optimal unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$, $55$, $57$, $58$ and $59$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Masaaki Harada

item.title: A new upper bound for the Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.29344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ denote the smallest integer such that every set of $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ points in the plane in general position contains $n$ points in convex position. In 1935, Erd\H{o}s and Szekeres conjectured that $\mathrm{ES}(n)=2^{n-2}+1$, and in 1960, they established the corresponding lower bound. A breakthrough on the upper bound was achieved by Suk in 2017, who proved that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{2/3}\log n)}. \] In this article, we further improve the upper bound by showing that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{1/3})}. \]
item.dc:creator: Yifan Hu, Guokuan Shao, Guozhen Shen

item.title: Extremal adjacency and distance spectral radii of graph powers
item.description: arXiv:2611.29397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and let $G^k$ denote its $k$-th power. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, \[ \rho(G^k)\geq \rho(P_n^k) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \rho_D(G^k)\leq \rho_D(P_n^k), \] where $P_n$ is the path of order $n$, and $\rho$ and $\rho_D$ are the adjacency and distance spectral radii, respectively. If $n\geq k+2$, equality in either inequality holds precisely when $G\cong P_n$. If $n\leq k+1$, every connected graph of order $n$ has complete $k$-th power, and both inequalities are equalities. The adjacency bound is proved by transferring a terminal vertex between pendant paths and applying a reflection rearrangement to a Rayleigh quotient. For the distance bound, a transfer of an entire pendant path is required; a Schur-complement comparison and estimates for the antisymmetric subspace of a path-power distance matrix yield the result. We also give examples showing why the two adjacency arguments do not extend directly to the distance spectral radius.
item.dc:creator: Joyentanuj Das, Anto Jerrin Ashni R, Sangeetha C

item.title: The mean orders of even and odd permutations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare the sums of the orders of the even and odd permutations of a given degree. For all large degrees the odd permutations have the larger sum. The excess equals the sum of orders of the permutations of odd order up to a relative error decaying faster than any power of the degree. Following Goh and Schmutz, we determine the logarithm of this sum over the group order asymptotically, with an explicit constant. Hence the ratio of the sums of element orders of the symmetric and alternating groups tends to two from above. The proof rests on an exact identity for generating functions. It isolates cycles of length a large prime times a small factor. Inclusion and exclusion over small odd primes enlarges this family. Each Euler factor is bounded by its maximum modulus. All constants are certified in ball arithmetic. Exact values up to degree 150 suggest that the odd permutations have the larger sum from degree four on.
item.dc:creator: Manoj Kumar Singh

item.title: On the 0-Rotatability of Regular Spider Trees of Leg Length 4
item.description: arXiv:2611.29448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A tree $T$ on $q$ edges is said to be $0$-rotatable if for every vertex $v \in V(T)$, there exists a graceful labeling $f : V(T) \to \{0, 1, \dots, q\}$ such that $f(v) = 0$. Rofa proved that all regular (symmetric) spider trees with leg length at most $3$ are $0$-rotatable and conjectured that the property holds for every leg length. In this note, we settle the first open case of this conjecture by proving that every regular spider tree $T(k, 4)$ with $k \ge 1$ legs of length $4$ is $0$-rotatable. Our proof combines Rofa's algebraic graceful labeling at the root with complementary labelings, an end-to-end leg-reversal construction placing $0$ at a leaf, and a two-leg reflection permutation placing $0$ at distance $2$ from the root.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Rofa

item.title: An asymptotic form of Thomasse's directed path conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.29486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thomass\'e conjectured that every oriented graph of minimum out-degree $d$ contains a directed path of length $2d$. We resolve this conjecture asymptotically by proving that every such graph contains a directed path of length at least $2d-O(d\log\log d/\log d)$.
item.dc:creator: Xinyao Ren, Yisai Xue, Ai Yang

item.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.29504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A connected graph of order at least $2k+2$ is {\em $k$-extendable} if it has a matching of size $k$ and every such matching extends to a perfect matching. In particular, a 1-extendable graph is also called a {\em matching covered graph}. A $k$-extendable graph $G$ is {\em minimal} if $G-e$ is not $k$-extendable for every $e\in E(G)$. Lov\'asz and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 23 (1977), 127--138] proved that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge6$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(3|V(G)|-6)/2$, and this bound is sharp for every even order at least 6. Fabres, Kothari and Carvalho [J. Graph Theory 96 (2021), 490--509] proved that every minimal 2-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge12$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(5|V(G)|-20)/2$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (2026), 559--606] characterized minimal matching covered bipartite graphs $G$ with $|E(G)|=(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ in terms of special trees. They also conjectured that, for every integer $k\ge1$, there exists an integer $N_k\le4k^2+2k$ such that every minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge N_k$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(2k+1)(|V(G)|-2k)/2$. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for $k\ge3$ and prove that the upper bound is sharp for every even order at least $6k$ ($k\ge3$).
item.dc:creator: Xiaoling He

item.title: Pieri formula for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of flag manifolds of type $A$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Pieri formula for the quantum product of an arbitrary opposite Schubert class with the opposite Schubert class associated to the cyclic permutation of the form $c[k,p]=(k-p+1,\ldots,k+1)$ in the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory ring of the (full) flag manifold $Fl_n = SL_n(\C)/B$. In this formula, the quantum product is expressed as a sum over $k$-Pieri chains in the quantum Bruhat graph on $S_n$. We give the coefficient of each $k$-Pieri chain in terms of the first components of its labels and the descents among labels with the same second component. By setting all equivariant parameters equal to $1$, the coefficient of a nonempty $k$-Pieri chain becomes the signed number of its $p$-markings.
item.dc:creator: Satoshi Naito, Khanh Nguyen Duc, Daisuke Sagaki

item.title: The Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.29517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In their 2007 paper on the log-convexity of combinatorial sequences, Liu and Wang conjectured that the Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity. We completely solve their conjecture by showing that this transformation preserves strong $q$-log-convexity. More generally, we provide a sufficient condition for a linear transformation, defined by a triangular array satisfying a certain three-term recurrence relation, to preserve strong $q$-log-convexity. As applications, we show that both the $r$-colored Eulerian transformation and the $m$-Stirling Eulerian transformation preserve strong $q$-log-convexity. In particular, we confirm a conjecture due to Liu and Zhu, which states that the Eulerian transformation of type $B$ preserves log-convexity.
item.dc:creator: Huihua Gao, Xin-Bei Liu, Weilin Wang

item.title: Universal Implications Among $k$-Prime Graph Labelings
item.description: arXiv:2611.29669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $k\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_k$ be the class of graphs admitting a bijective labeling by consecutive integers beginning at $k$, with coprime labels at adjacent vertices. We determine all universal inclusions between distinct such classes: $\mathcal P_i\subseteq\mathcal P_j$ holds for $i\ne j$ if and only if $(i,j)=(2,1)$ or $(3,1)$. In particular, the classes are pairwise distinct. The proof translates universal inclusion into a spanning-embedding question for coprimality graphs on consecutive integer intervals. Edge-count identities, arithmetic-progression estimates, and prime-residue switching exclude all other inclusions; a prime-gap argument reduces the remaining finite range to fifteen explicit rational inequalities. We further show that, for each nonexceptional ordered pair, the graph orders at which edge counts obstruct inclusion have a positive natural density. This density is described through a limiting distribution of correlated Euler products, for which we give an atomlessness argument. The classification resolves the distinct-index formulation of the universal-implication conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Jing Zhang, Yuan Li

item.title: Unary maps are restrictions of linear maps and $k$-ary maps are restrictions of homogeneous maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.29718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study maps on a finite set $S$ under renaming elements of $S$ and extending $S$. We show that every unary map is linear and every $k$-ary map is homogeneous with respect to such renamings and embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Roman Bacik

item.title: Counting Eulerian Orientations in Regular Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.29726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a pseudograph, and let $\varepsilon(G)$ denote the number of Eulerian orientations of $G$. Lieb and Wu, and later Schrijver, showed that if $G$ has degree sequence $(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_n)$, where each $d_i$ is a positive even integer, then \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \prod_{i = 1}^n 2^{-d_i/2} \binom{d_i}{d_i/2}.\] Schrijver conjectured that for simple $d$-regular graphs, $\varepsilon(G)\leq\varepsilon(K_{d+1})^{n/(d+1)}$, with equality attained by disjoint unions of cliques of order $d+1$. In this paper, we prove a multigraph bound that implies the known case $d=4$, and we also improve Schrijver's lower bound for $d$-regular graphs, using an inductive relation between $\varepsilon(G)$ and the number $\ell_i(G)$ of cycles of each possible length $i \geq 1$ in $G$. We define \[ \ell(G) = \sum_{i = 1}^n \frac{\ell_i(G)}{(d - 1)^i}\] and we prove with $\lambda = (d - 1)\log(1 + 1/(d - 1))$ that for all $d \geq 2$, \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \exp(\lambda \ell(G)) \cdot S_d(n),\] where $S_d(n)$ denotes $2^{-dn/2}\binom{d}{d/2}^n$. The bound sharply improves the lower bound of Lieb, Wu and Schrijver, and gives good estimates for $\varepsilon(G)$ for various graphs, such as integer lattices. The bound is almost tight for random regular graphs, and we conjecture for each even $d \geq 4$ that there exists a constant $c_d > 0$ such that $\varepsilon(G) \leq \exp(c_d\lambda \ell(G)) \cdot S_d(n)$ for every $n$-vertex $d$-regular pseudograph.
item.dc:creator: Srinjoy Srimani, Jacques Verstraete, Jason Yang

item.title: The probability that two random generalized derangements have the same number of cycles
item.description: arXiv:2611.29746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using singularity analysis, we show that the probability that two independently and uniformly selected generalized derangements of size $n$ have the same number of cycles is asymptotically the same as the corresponding probability for unrestricted permutations, namely, $\sim \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi\log n}}\;.$
item.dc:creator: Dmitrii Smorchkov, Mikl\'os B\'ona

item.title: Commutative bishuffle algebras and Pattern Avoidance
item.description: arXiv:2611.29782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces the notion of a commutative bishuffle algebra, that linearizes classical pattern avoidance. The free commutative bishuffle algebra on one generator has a basis of permutations, divisibility of monomials is pattern containment, and the classes of permutations avoiding given patterns are the monomial bases of its quotients by monomial ideals. This free algebra is not Noetherian, but we show that its quotient by the antisymmetrizer $e_k$ is Noetherian for every $k$, and we conjecture that the same holds for its quotient by any nonzero ideal stable under the symmetric groups, in analogy with the Specht problem. We develop Gr\"obner bases for ideals of the free algebra and prove that the elements $e_k\oplus\tau$, with $\tau$ ranging over any set of permutations, form a Gr\"obner basis for the lexicographic ordering and for its opposite. This gives an algebraic form of the theorem of Backelin, West and Xin: the permutations avoiding all $k\cdots21\oplus\tau$ and those avoiding all $12\cdots k\oplus\tau$ are two monomial bases of one and the same quotient.
item.dc:creator: Anton Khoroshkin

item.title: Parity-safe digraphs with countably many ends are kernel-perfect
item.description: arXiv:2611.29786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set that every other vertex points into, and a digraph is kernel-perfect if every induced subgraph has a kernel. A digraph without odd cycles in which no ray contains infinitely many vertices that each send an infinite fan of disjoint paths to that ray is safe. The conjecture that every safe digraph is kernel-perfect was proved earlier for digraphs with finitely many ends. We prove a stronger statement for at most countably many ends. Number the vertices of a ray, and let the type of a path that ends on the ray be the parity of the sum of its length and the number of its last vertex. A fan is mixed if it has infinitely many paths of each type, and a digraph is parity-safe if it has no odd cycle and no ray containing infinitely many vertices with a mixed fan to it. Yablo's graph (omega,<) is not parity-safe. Its variant with edges only between vertices of different parity has a kernel - it is parity-safe but not safe. Our main result is that a parity-safe digraph with at most countably many ends is kernel-perfect, and the claim for safe digraphs follows since safety implies parity-safety. The digraph may have any cardinality, and nothing is assumed about the structure of the ends, but the case of uncountably many ends remains open.
item.dc:creator: Sjur Dyrkolbotn, Michal Walicki

item.title: General bounds for metric dimension of diameter-two graphs with applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.29819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the metric dimension of several classes of graphs with diameter two. First, we establish a general lower bound for the metric dimension of graphs with diameter two in terms of their order and maximum degree. We then apply our results to Grassmann graphs, Moore graphs, and bilinear forms graphs. For Kneser graphs, we obtain new upper bounds, while for $G_q(n,2)$ Grassmann graphs we establish new upper bounds provided by constructions of resolving sets. For Moore graphs of diameter two, we derive improved lower bounds, and for $H_q(n,2)$ bilinear forms graphs, we obtain new upper and lower bounds on their metric dimension.
item.dc:creator: \'Akos Beke

item.title: Cylindrical dimers and monomial immanants
item.description: arXiv:2611.29860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a bipartite graph on a cylinder, group its perfect matchings by homological height and sum their weights in each group. We prove that every minor of the resulting Toeplitz matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the edge weights, settling a question recorded by Lai. We first prove conjectures of Galashin and the author concerning directed cycles in cylindrical networks, and then deduce the dimer theorem from them. A related, stronger positivity property for superpositions of cylindrical matchings turns out to be equivalent to Stembridge's interval-product conjecture on monomial immanants. Using annular webs, we prove this conjecture for partitions with at most four columns. A stretching argument extends this to all partitions with parts in $\{n,2n,3n,4n\}$.
item.dc:creator: Pavlo Pylyavskyy

item.title: Parking Functions inspired by board games
item.description: arXiv:2611.29890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce two new parking schemes inspired by the classic board games Monopoly and backgammon. We consider a one-way street with $n$ parking spots and a queue of $n$ cars waiting to park. Each car has a preferred parking spot and enters in sequence to park. Under the Monopoly parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. Under the backgammon parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it bumps the already parked car out of that spot and takes its place. The bumped car then returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. A preference list is a parking function for a given parking scheme if all cars successfully park under that scheme. We prove that all preference lists are parking functions under both the Monopoly and backgammon parking schemes. However, the final parking order differs significantly between the two schemes. For a fixed permutation $\pi$, we provide a product formula for the number of Monopoly parking functions resulting in the outcome $\pi$. Analogously, we show that the number of backgammon parking functions with outcome $\pi$ is bounded below by $2^{n-1}$ and bounded above by the $n$-th Catalan number. We also obtain exact formulas involving Motzkin numbers for several families of outcomes. We define the displacement of a car as the absolute difference between the spot where a car ultimately parks and its preferred spot. Displacement multisets encode the displacements for cars with nonzero displacement. We provide formulas for the number of backgammon parking functions with a fixed displacement multiset of cardinality at most $2$, as well as for the number of Monopoly parking functions whose displacement multiset is a given singleton set. We conclude with some directions for further research.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Clifton, Pamela E. Harris, Maryam Khaqan

item.title: An Exact Vertex Localization of Zykov's Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.30029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a vertex-based localization of the exact form of Zykov's theorem. For a graph $G$ of order $n\geq1$, let $N(G,K_t)$ denote its number of copies of $K_t$, and let $c(v)$ be the order of a largest clique containing $v$. Write $Z_t(n,s)=N(T_s(n),K_t)$, where $T_s(n)$ is the balanced complete $s$-partite graph on $n$ vertices. We prove that, for every integer $t\geq2$, \[ N(G,K_t)\leq \frac1n\sum_{v\in V(G)}Z_t(n,c(v)). \] Equality holds if and only if $G$ is $K_t$-free or $G\cong T_s(n)$ for some $t\leq s\leq n$. Moreover, the coefficients $Z_t(n,s)$ are pointwise best possible among all bounds of this form. Our result strengthens the previous vertex-localized bound \[ N(G,K_t)\leq n^{t-1} \sum_{v\in V(G)} \frac{\binom{c(v)}{t}}{c(v)^t} \] by accounting for the integer part sizes of Tur\'an graphs. The comparison between the two upper bounds is strict precisely when some vertex $v$ satisfies $c(v)\geq t$ and $c(v)\nmid n$. As consequences, we recover the exact Zykov and Tur\'an bounds without divisibility assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Adak, L. Sunil Chandran

item.title: A Constructive Lower Bound for the Growth Constant of Ternary Cap Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.30110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $r_3(d)$ denote the maximum size of a cap set in $\mathbb{F}_3^d$. We prove that the exponential growth constant $\Lambda = \lim_{d\to\infty} r_3(d)^{1/d}$ is strictly greater than $2.22920646813$. The main advance comes from combining two-color recursive synchronization with cross-layer joint filling of a seven-dimensional local alphabet that contains collinear triples (lines). By encoding marked positions as $14$-step closed walks on a two-state directed graph, any zero-sum triple with a fixed outermost color is forced to choose the identical closed walk---and hence the identical record---at every recursive layer, at a net cost of $1000$ dimensions per level. Because the open seven-dimensional coordinates are deferred to the outermost layer, all positions of the same type across all layers can be pooled per record and filled jointly via grouped binary-flag nodes. A $2\times 2$ transfer matrix governs the weighted record count, and spectral dominance over two tilted tail matrices converts this count into a capacity lower bound. Feeding each resulting bound back into the filling parameters iteratively amplifies the growth rate, while a companion-path score exclusion test further enlarges the admissible walk family. The final bound is certified by finite enumeration and exact integer comparisons.
item.dc:creator: ZeHua Lu

item.title: Reverse Schensted bumping, inverse reduction map and concatenation in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection
item.description: arXiv:2611.30132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Provided the explicit formula for the inverse reduction map, arXiv:2606.24840, we exhibit for symplectic bumped intervals and for symplectic bumped columns disjoint for the action of the parity involution, the feasibility of the concatenation operation to return a semi-standard tableau in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection
item.dc:creator: Olga Azenhas

item.title: Compatible expansions and rigidity in subtraction games with a single pass
item.description: arXiv:2611.30147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study normal-play subtraction games with one globally shared pass. An expansion of the subtraction set is pass-equivalent if it leaves the pass-available Sprague--Grundy sequence unchanged. We show that pure periodicity of the ordinary sequence, together with an eventual translation identity for the pass-available sequence, forces every pass-equivalent expansion to preserve the ordinary sequence. For two-element sets $\{x,y\}$, we classify the compatible additional moves: they are exactly $x+1,\ldots,y-1$ when $y\leq 2x$, and there are none when $y>2x$. We extend this result to sets in short intervals. An exact recurrence certificate also exhibits a three-element set for which pass-state rigidity fails.
item.dc:creator: Richard M. Low

item.title: Products of translates: bounds and constructions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study products of translates of the form $(A+d)(A+d)$ with $d\in D$, where both $A$ and $D$ are finite subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. We show that $|(A+a)(A+a)|\ge C|A|^{5/3}$ for some $a\in A$, and that $|(A+D)(A+D)|\le |A|^{2-c(\alpha)}$ for some $c(\alpha)>0$ when $|D|=|A|^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha<1$.
item.dc:creator: Sian Fang, Danqing He, Xinyu Zhu

item.title: A construction of proper Jordan schemes of rank $5$
item.description: arXiv:2611.30231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q$ be a prime power such that $m=q^2+q+1$ is a prime satisfying $m\equiv 1\pmod{4}$. We construct a proper symmetric Jordan scheme of rank $5$ on $2m$ vertices using a Singer difference set with parameters $(m,q+1,1)$ and the Paley graph on $m$ vertices.
item.dc:creator: Sho Suda

item.title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$. In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$. More precisely, we independently label lower-dimensional faces and use the palette to exclude prescribed red configurations, while a container argument controls the size of blue cliques. As a first application of our theorem, we obtain \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)>2^{\Omega_k(n\log n)}\). Combined with the upper bound due to Mubayi and Suk, this yields \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)=2^{\Theta_k(n\log n)}\), where \(B^{(k)}\) is the half-graph. This answers in the affirmative a question posed by Mubayi and Suk. As a second application of our theorem, we show $r_k(k+1,3;n)=2^{\Theta_k(n^{k-2}\log n)}$, which, together with a new stepping-up lemma developed in this paper, further yields $r_k(k+1,t;n)=\twr_{t-1}(\Theta_{k,t}(n^{k-t+1}\log n))$ for every fixed $k\ge6$ and $4\le t\le k-2$, where $\twr_1(x)=x$ and $\twr_{j+1}(x)=2^{\twr_j(x)}$. Here $r_k(k+1,t;n)$ denotes the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the $k$-subsets of an $N$-vertex set contains either $k+1$ vertices spanning at least $t$ red edges or a blue clique of order $n$. As a third application of our theorem, we show that $r_k(F_{\ell,k,d},n)>2^{\Omega_{k,\ell,d}(n^{k-d-2}\log n)}$ for all fixed integers $k\ge4$, $1\le d\le k-3$, and $\ell\ge2k+1$ with $k\nmid\ell$, where $F_{\ell,k,d}$ is obtained from the $k$-uniform tight cycle of length $\ell$ by deleting $d$ consecutive edges.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhi Bai, Xinyu Hu, Kaidi Liu, Guanghui Wang

item.title: Alpha-points of a putative binary $q$-analog of the Fano plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.30333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A point $P$ of a putative $q$-analog $\mathcal{D}$ of the Fano plane is an $\alpha$-point if the derived design of $\mathcal{D}$ in $P$ is a Desarguesian line spread. Kiermaier showed that for $q$ prime or even every hyperplane contains a point which is not an $\alpha$-point. For $q=2$ we study the $45$ blocks of $\mathcal{D}$ inside a hyperplane $H$. Call a $5$-subspace of $H$ a $\beta$-flat if all its blocks pass through one point, its focal point. We show that at least $41$ points of $H$ are not focal points of $\beta$-flats. Consequently $\mathcal{D}$ has at least $85$ non-$\alpha$-points, at most $42$ $\alpha$-points, and at most $22$ $\alpha$-points in every hyperplane.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Kurz

item.title: Consecutive sums and Reconstructing Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.30462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study several problems concerning consecutive sums of integer sequences and their relationship with Sidon sets. We also provide new lower bounds for an extremal function related to sequences with distinct consecutive sums, and consider reconstruction problems from multisets of consecutive sums.
item.dc:creator: Norbert Hegyv\'ari, P\'eter P\'al Pach, Quanyu Tang

item.title: A one-third bound for domination in cubic graphs of girth at least six
item.description: arXiv:2611.30512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $S$ has a neighbor in $S$. The domination number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set of $G$. In 2010, Verstra\"{e}te conjectured that every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$ and girth at least six satisfies $\gamma(G)\le n/3$. More recently, Dorbec and Henning established this bound under the additional assumption that $G$ contains neither a $7$-cycle nor an $8$-cycle. We prove Verstra\"{e}te's conjecture in full. As a corollary, we settle the $C_4$-free case of Kostochka's conjecture, which asserts that the same bound holds for all cubic bipartite graphs.
item.dc:creator: Kun Cheng, Changlong Shen, Leilei Zhang

item.title: On \(q\)-ary Minimal Linear Codes from Hierarchical Posets
item.description: arXiv:2611.30551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study several families of \(q\)-ary linear codes constructed from two-level hierarchical posets over finite fields \(\mathbb{F}_q\), where \(q>2\). By using generating functions and additive characters, we determine their complete weight distributions, dimensions, and minimum distances. This paper focuses on constructing minimal codes that violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition. By analyzing the weight distributions and support sets of the codewords, we show that a large class of the constructed codes are minimal and strictly violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.
item.dc:creator: Wen Ma

item.title: The Hamilton cycle space in the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process
item.description: arXiv:2611.30619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G(n,m)$ denote the graph at step $m$ of the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process on $n$ vertices. The process starts with the edgeless graph and adds one edge at each step, chosen uniformly at random from the missing edges. Let $\tau_3$ be the first step at which the minimum degree of $G(n,m)$ reaches three. We answer a question of Christoph, Nenadov and Petrova [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 176 (2026) 254--267] by proving that, as $n$ tends to infinity through odd integers, with high probability the Hamilton cycles of $G(n,m)$ span its cycle space over $\Ftwo$ simultaneously for all $m\ge\tau_3$. On the same event, $G(n,m)$ is Hamilton-connected for every $m\ge\tau_3$.
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhang, Wensheng Sun, Panpan Cheng

item.title: Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments
item.description: arXiv:2611.30684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings. This model specializes to the partial matching model for the mixed moments of continuous $q$-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we consider the corresponding multivariate moments and prove that their minimal numerators have nonnegative coefficients up to an explicit sign.
item.dc:creator: Younggwang Cho

item.title: A variant of the Erd\H{o}s--Gy\'arf\'as problem for $K_9$ and $K_{12}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.30718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $H$, let $r_H(n)$ be the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of $K_n$ such that every copy of $H$ contains a color appearing an odd number of times. We prove that $r_{K_9}(n)\le\exp(O((\log n)^{2/3}))$ and $r_{K_{12}}(n)\le\exp(O((\log n)^{2/3}))$. These bounds on $r_H(n)$ yield linear graph codes of density at least $\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$ that avoid images of $K_9$ and $K_{12}$.
item.dc:creator: Luyi Li, Guiying Yan, Zicheng Ye

item.title: Partition rank and analytic rank over finite field
item.description: arXiv:2611.30721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the partition rank and the analytic rank of a tensor over any finite field are equivalent up to a constant depending only on the order of the tensor. The proof combines Mili\'cevi\'c's theorem on dense multilinear varieties with the differential Schur complement of Moshkovitz and Zhu. The new ingredient is a method for approximately eliminating multilinear equations.
item.dc:creator: Qiyuan Chen, Ke Ye

item.title: Joint statistics on vexillary involutions via Fulton's essential set
item.description: arXiv:2611.30791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We jointly enumerate various statistics over vexillary involutions among which there are the number of descents and the number of peaks. As a by-product, we get an equidistribution result between vexillary involutions and 3412-avoiding involutions, which, notably, implies that, for every $n$ and $k$, the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $3412$ and having $k$ descents equals the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $2143$ and having $k$ ascents. The proof describes $2143$-avoiding involutions through Fulton's ranked essential set, translates the count into a weighted enumeration of walks in the quarter plane, and solves the latter explicitly. Finally, we show that arbitrary vexillary permutations are encoded by excursions of the same walk model.
item.dc:creator: Niccol\`o Castronuovo

item.title: The spectrum of codegree Tur\'an densities of 3-graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.30861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The \emph{minimum codegree} $\delta_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Tur\'an density} $\gamma(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $\delta_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $\alpha\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Tur\'an density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_\alpha$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $\gamma(\mathcal{F}')>\alpha$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_\alpha$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Tur\'an spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independently of us.) We also consider \emph{positive codegree Tur\'an density}, defined analogously by taking the minimum only over $(k-1)$-sets contained in at least one edge. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c<1$ such that, for every integer $k\geq3$, every real number in $[c,1)$ is the positive codegree Tur\'an density of a $k$-graph family. This is done by presenting a construction with a relatively short proof, without optimising the value of $c$.
item.dc:creator: Jun Gao, Oleg Pikhurko, Mingyuan Rong, Shumin Sun

item.title: The number of non-isomorphic spanning trees in regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.30899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By a classical theorem of Otter, the number of non-isomorphic trees on $n$ vertices is $\alpha^n\exp(-o(n))$, where $\alpha\approx 2.956$ is Otter's constant. We prove that every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices contains $\alpha^n\exp(-o_d(n))$ non-isomorphic spanning trees, where $o_d(n)/n\to0$ as $d\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Csongor Beke

item.title: $k$-ary Legendre pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.31067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $k$-ary Legendre pairs and derive arithmetic restrictions on their existence and balance. For an odd prime $p$, we determine the component sums of a $p$-ary Legendre pair and show that, after normalization, each component has fixed symbol composition. As a consequence, every $p$-ary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ yields a Butson Hadamard matrix $H(2p,2\ell+2)$. For ternary Legendre pairs we combine fixed-content necklaces, integral-PAF symmetries, exact half-frequency restrictions, compression-decompression, and PSD tests. These reductions lead to ternary Legendre pairs for every admissible length $\ell\le32$. We conjecture that ternary Legendre pairs exist for every admissible length.
item.dc:creator: Ilias S. Kotsireas, Huaning Liu, Arne Winterhof

item.title: A quasi-tree expansion for the two variable Bollob\'as--Riordan polynomial using a single basepoint
item.description: arXiv:2611.31070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a quasi-tree expansion formula for the two variable Bollob\'as--Riordan polynomial of ribbon graphs that uses a single basepoint (a point on the boundary of the ribbon graph) as auxiliary datum.
item.dc:creator: Anita Dalma P\'ah\'an, Lilla T\'othm\'er\'esz

item.title: A Characterization of Tangle Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.31121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a matroid with at least two elements is a tangle matroid if and only if it cannot be covered by three hyperplanes. Some consequences of this theorem are also noted. In particular, no binary matroid of rank at least two is a tangle matroid.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Hall

item.title: Common tiles from fractional tiles for two lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.31136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $L_1, L_2\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be lattices of the same volume and let $D_1, D_2$ be two bounded fundamental domains for $L_1, L_2$. We show that there is a measurable common tile for $L_1$ and $L_2$ contained in $D_1+D_2$. The main tool is a result of Bowen, Kun and Sabok (2021) which shows how to obtain a measurable perfect matching given a fractional perfect matching in hyperfinite graphings.
item.dc:creator: Jan Greb\'ik, Mihail N. Kolountzakis

item.title: Reduction types of curves in tame extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $C/K$ be a curve of genus $g\geq 1$ over a discretely valued field $K$ with algebraically closed residue field. In this paper, we study the behaviour of the reduction type of $C$ under finite tame extensions. If $L/K$ is a tame extension of degree $n$, we give sufficient conditions on the reduction type $R$ of $C$ so that the reduction type of the base change $C_L$ is uniquely determined by $R$ and $n$. In particular, if $C$ has abelian and toric ranks zero, then $R$ satisfies these conditions. We also give an algorithm to compute the possibilities for the reduction type of $C_L$ given only $R$ and $n$. The main method involves studying harmonic covers of graphs with a cyclic action. As a result, we obtain a characterisation of tame curves with potentially good reduction in terms of their reduction type, and a new proof of a result by Liu-Lorenzini-Raynaud regarding the non-realisability of certain reduction types.
item.dc:creator: J\'ulia Mart\'inez-Mar\'in

item.title: A filtered basis for Haiman ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.28264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given the polynomial ring $R=\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n, y_1, \dots, y_n]$, we consider the Haiman ideal $J(d)$ of polynomials that vanish to order $d$ on the diagonals. We define a rotational order on monomials and use it to construct a filtration on $J(d)$ and a bigraded, homogeneous, free $\mathbb{C}[\mathbf{y}]$-basis compatible with this filtration. This gives a new independent proof that $J(d)$ is free over $y$'s. We also discuss the connections between this filtration and triply-graded link homology.
item.dc:creator: Joshua P. Turner

item.title: The M\"obius Homology Laplacian for Persistence Modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.28292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Persistent homology provides a framework for studying the evolution of topological features across filtered spaces. While persistence diagrams give discrete invariants that record the birth and death of homological features, they do not directly encode analytic or geometric structure associated to persistence modules. This paper develops a spectral framework for persistent homology by introducing and studying a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex, called the M\"obius homology Laplacian. M\"obius homology categorifies M\"obius inversion for persistence modules by replacing integer-valued data with vector-space-valued chain complexes. By equipping these chain complexes with inner products, we define a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex whose kernel provides canonical cycle representatives for the associated M\"obius homology space. We analyze the spectral properties of this operator in two primary settings: one-parameter persistence modules and birth-death modules arising from filtrations of simplicial complexes. For one-parameter modules, we completely characterize the eigenvalues of the degree-one M\"obius homology Laplacian. For birth-death modules, we show that the trace and determinant of the degree-zero M\"obius homology Laplacian reflect the combinatorial structure of the persistence diagram.
item.dc:creator: Tatum Rask

item.title: Improved bounds for the binary Chowla conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.28392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the M\"obius function $\mu$ and every fixed $0 < \epsilon < 1$, we prove \[ \sum_{n \le x} \mu(n) \mu(n + 1) \ll_{\epsilon} \frac{x}{(\log x)^{1 - \epsilon}}. \] This improves on OpenAI's recent bound of $x/(\log x)^c$, where $c > 0$ is a tiny absolute constant. The proof echoes the graph expansion framework of Helfgott, Radziwill, and Pilatte on the logarithmic Chowla conjecture, earlier Fourier analytic methods of Matom\"aki, Radziwill, and Tao on the Chowla conjecture on average, as well as work of Ter\"av\"ainen and the author for M\"obius on shifted primes. This also yields an improved result, \[ \sum_{p \le x} \mu(p + 2) \ll_{\epsilon} \frac{\pi(x)}{(\log x)^{1/2 - \epsilon}}. \] Specifically, we refine the determinant approach from the Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors. We replace the averaged prime weights of L\"u-Wang-Wu with an exact partition of prime intervals. Once sieving out exceptional integers, this enables uniform cancellation with arbitrary log power savings.
item.dc:creator: Jared Duker Lichtman

item.title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
item.description: arXiv:2611.28496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--R\"odl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $\sigma_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence. In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-R\"odl theorem.
item.dc:creator: Sohail Farhangi

item.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.28533v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[ |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Albert Cochrane, Todd Cochrane, Craig Spencer

item.title: The Sch\"urmann-Vallentin lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering in dimension six
item.description: arXiv:2611.28562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ discovered by Sch\"urmann and Vallentin in 2006 is the unique (up to similarity) six-dimensional lattice that gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Garber
