item.dc:creator: Kinkar Chandra Das, Ali Ghalavand, Ali Reza Ashrafi

item.title: Approximating TSP walks in subcubic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2112.06278v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every simple 2-connected subcubic graph on $n$ vertices with $n_2$ vertices of degree 2 has a TSP walk of length at most $\frac{5n+n_2}{4}-1$, confirming a conjecture of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Kr\'al', and Mohar. This bound is best possible; there are infinitely many subcubic and cubic graphs whose minimum TSP walks have lengths $\frac{5n+n_2}{4}-1$ and $\frac{5n}{4} - 2$ respectively. We characterize the extremal subcubic examples meeting this bound. We also give a quadratic-time combinatorial algorithm for finding such a TSP walk. In particular, we obtain a $\frac{5}{4}$-approximation algorithm for the graphic TSP on simple cubic graphs, improving on the previously best known approximation ratio of $\frac{9}{7}$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B 158 (2023), 70-104
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Wigal, Youngho Yoo, Xingxing Yu

item.title: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2402.19351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomass\'e. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Combinatorial Theory Series B 182 (2027), 106-125
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Bessy, Daniel Gon\c{c}alves, Amadeus Reinald

item.title: Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions
item.description: arXiv:2408.15075v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We enumerate the numbers $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324)$ of 1324-avoiding $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ inversions for all $k$ and $n \geq (k+7)/2$. The result depends on a structural characterization of such permutations in terms of a new notion of almost-decomposability. In particular, our enumeration verifies half of a conjecture of Claesson, Jel\'inek and Steingr\'imsson, according to which $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324) \leq \mathrm{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)$ for all $n$ and $k$. Proving also the other half would improve the best known upper bound for the exponential growth rate of the number of $1324$-avoiders from $13.5$ to approximately $13.002$.
item.dc:creator: Svante Linusson, Emil Verkama

item.title: The ring of stable characters over $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2409.16571v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a fixed prime power $q$, let $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$ denote the family of groups $\text{GL}_N(q)$ for $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of "stable" class functions of $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$, and show it admits four different linear bases, each arising naturally in different settings. One such basis is that of stable irreducible characters, namely, the class functions spanned by the characters corresponding to finitely generated simple $\mathrm{VI}$-modules in the sense of [arXiv:1408.3694,arXiv:1602.00654]. A second one comes from characters of parabolic representations. The final two, one originally defined in [arXiv:1803.04155] and the other in [arXiv:2110.11099], are more combinatorial in nature. As corollaries, we clarify many properties of these four bases and prove a conjecture from [arXiv:2106.11587].
item.dc:creator: Danielle Ernst-West, Doron Puder, Yotam Shomroni

item.title: Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2412.19560v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A long-standing Conjecture of S. Negami states that a connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane. It is known that the Conjecture is equivalent to the fact that \emph{the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ has no finite planar cover}. We prove three theorems showing that the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ admits no planar cover with certain structural properties, and that the minimal planar cover of $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ (if it exists) must be $4$-connected.
item.dc:creator: Dickson Y. B. Annor, Yuri Nikolayevsky, Michael S. Payne

item.title: A Generalization of Ramanujan's Sum over Finite Rings
item.description: arXiv:2505.09996v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalization of Ramanujan sums over finite rings and derive an explicit formula for these sums. These generalized Ramanujan sums coincide with the eigenvalues of the unitary Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(R,R^{\times})$, as follows from Babai's result on Cayley graph spectra. This provides a useful approach to determining the spectrum of the unitary Cayley graph. Moreover, under a certain independence condition on the maximal left ideals, we show that our formula extends the classical formula for Ramanujan sums to finite rings.
item.dc:creator: Priya Dhankhar, Sanjay Kumar Singh

item.title: An Introduction to Algebraic Combinatorics
item.description: arXiv:2506.00738v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is an introduction to algebraic combinatorics, written for a quarter-long graduate course. It starts with a rigorous introduction to formal power series with some combinatorial applications, then discusses integer partitions (proving Jacobi's triple product identity), permutations (Lehmer codes, cycles) and subtractive methods (alternating sums, cancellations and inclusion-exclusion principles, with a particular focus on sign-reversing involutions and determinants). The last chapter introduces symmetric polynomials and proves the Littlewood--Richardson rule using Bender--Knuth involutions (a la Stembridge). The appendix contains over 200 exercises (without solutions).
item.dc:creator: Darij Grinberg

item.title: Infinite polynomial patterns in large subsets of the rational numbers
item.description: arXiv:2506.19667v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Inspired by a question of Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson, we prove two new results about infinite polynomial configurations in large subsets of the rational numbers. First, given a finite coloring of $\mathbb{Q}$, we show that there exists an infinite set $B = \{b_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}$ such that $$\{b_i, b_i^2 + b_j : i < j\}$$ is monochromatic. Second, we prove that every subset of positive density in the rational numbers contains a translate of such an infinite configuration. The corresponding results in the integers are both known to be false, so our results provide natural and relatively simple examples of combinatorial structures that distinguish between the Ramsey-theoretic properties of the rational numbers and the integers. The proofs of our main results build upon methods developed in a series of papers by Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson to translate from combinatorics into dynamics, where the core of the argument reduces to understanding the behavior of certain polynomial ergodic averages. The new dynamical tools required for this analysis are a Wiener--Wintner theorem for polynomially-twisted ergodic averages in $\mathbb{Q}$-systems and a structure theorem for Abramov $\mathbb{Q}$-systems.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Ackelsberg

item.title: The Hamilton cycle space of random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2506.19731v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The cycle space of a graph $G$, denoted $\mathcal{C}(G)$, is a vector space over ${\mathbb F}_2$, spanned by all incidence vectors of edge-sets of cycles of $G$. If $G$ has $n$ vertices, then $\mathcal{C}_n(G)$ denotes the subspace of $\mathcal{C}(G)$, spanned by the incidence vectors of Hamilton cycles of $G$. A classical result in the theory of random graphs asserts that for $G \sim \mathbb{G}(n,p)$, asymptotically almost surely the necessary condition $\delta(G) \geq 2$ is also sufficient to ensure Hamiltonicity. Resolving a problem of Christoph, Nenadov, and Petrova, we augment this result by proving that $\mathcal{C}_n(G) = \mathcal{C}(G)$ holds asymptotically almost surely for $G \sim \mathbb{G}(n,p)$, with $n$ being odd and $p := p(n) \geq (\log n + 2 \log \log n + \omega(1))/n$. That is, not only does $G$ typically have a Hamilton cycle, but its Hamilton cycles are typically rich enough to span its cycle space. It is known and easy to show that if $p := p(n) \leq (\log n + 2 \log \log n - \omega(1))/n$, then a.a.s. $\mathcal{C}_n(G) \neq \mathcal{C}(G)$ unless $G$ is a forest.
item.dc:creator: Dan Hefetz, Michael Krivelevich

item.title: Hall--Littlewood expansions of chromatic quasisymmetric functions using linked rook placements
item.description: arXiv:2506.23082v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we obtain a Hall--Littlewood expansion of the chromatic quasisymmetric function arising from a natural unit interval order and describe the coefficients in terms of linked rook placements. Applying the Carlsson--Mellit relation between chromatic quasisymmetric functions and unicellular LLT polynomials, we also obtain a combinatorial description for the coefficients of the unicellular LLT polynomials expanded in terms of the modified transformed Hall--Littlewood polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Jang Soo Kim, Seung Jin Lee, Meesue Yoo

item.title: Fractional domatic number and minimum degree
item.description: arXiv:2508.19617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The domatic number of a graph $G$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dominating sets of $G$. We are interested in the LP-relaxation of this parameter, which is called the fractional domatic number of $G$. We study its extremal value in the class of graphs of minimum degree $d$. The fractional domatic number of a graph of minimum degree $d$ is always at most $d+1$, and at least $(1-o(1))\, d/\ln d$ as $d\to \infty$. This is asymptotically tight even within the class of split graphs. Our main result concerns the case $d=2$; we show that, excluding $8$ exceptional graphs, the fractional domatic number of every connected graph of minimum degree (at least) $2$ is at least $5/2$. We also show that this bound cannot be improved if only finitely many graphs are excluded, even for bipartite graphs of arbitrarily large girth. This proves in a stronger sense a conjecture by Gadouleau, Harms, Mertzios, and Zamaraev (2024). This also extends and generalises results from McCuaig and Shepherd (1989), from Fujita, Kameda, and Yamashita (2000), and from Abbas, Egerstedt, Liu, Thomas, and Whalen (2016). Finally, we show that graphs of sub-exponential expansion and sufficiently large girth $g$ have fractional domatic number $3 - o_g(1)$.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Chuet, Hugo Demaret, Hoang La, Fran\c{c}ois Pirot

item.title: Differential Equations for Macdonald's Hypergeometric Series
item.description: arXiv:2510.10875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study differential equations for certain multivariable hypergeometric series, introduced by Macdonald in the 1980s, which generalize hypergeometric functions of matrix argument due to Bochner and Herz. Such equations are well studied in the one-variable case, where they serve to characterize the classical hypergeometric functions $_p F_q(z)$ and provide a route to many of their key properties. Accordingly, Macdonald asked for a similar characterization for the multivariate series. This problem, however, has remained open. Differential equations are known only for a handful of cases with $p\leq 3$ and $q\leq 2$. In this paper we give a complete solution to Macdonald's problem. In the multivariable case there are \emph{two} series $_p F_q(x)$ and $_p F_q(x,y)$, depending on $p+q+1$ parameters and one or two sets of variables, $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $y=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$. We give differential equations characterizing both series, for all values of $p$ and $q$. The proof involves several new ideas in the theory of symmetric functions, especially Jack polynomials and interpolation polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Hong Chen, Siddhartha Sahi

item.title: Minimally tough series-parallel graphs with toughness at least $1/2$
item.description: arXiv:2512.01905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $t$ be a positive real number. A graph is called \emph{$t$-tough} if the removal of any vertex set $S$ that disconnects the graph leaves at most $|S|/t$ components. The toughness of a graph is the largest $t$ for which the graph is $t$-tough. A graph is minimally $t$-tough if the toughness of the graph is $t$, and the deletion of any edge from the graph decreases the toughness. Series--parallel graphs are graphs with two distinguished vertices called terminals, formed recursively by two simple composition operations, series and parallel joins. They can be used to model series and parallel electric circuits. We characterize minimally $t$-tough series--parallel graphs for all $t\ge 1/2$. It is clear that there is no minimally $t$-tough series--parallel graph if $t>1$. We show that, for $1\ge t >1/2$, most of the series--parallel graphs with toughness $t$ are minimally $t$-tough, but most of the series--parallel graphs with toughness $1/2$ are not minimally $1/2$-tough.
item.dc:creator: Gyula Y. Katona, Humara Khan

item.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. I
item.description: arXiv:2512.13437v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is the first in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. The Cullis' determinant is defined for every matrix of size $n\times k$, where $n \ge k \ge 1$ and is equal to the ordinary determinant if $n = k$. In this paper we solve the linear preserver problem for the Cullis' determinant for $k \ge 4, n \ge k + 2$ and $n + k$ is even. It appears that in this case all linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant are non-singular and could be represented by two-sided matrix multiplication. Note that the cases where $n = k$ or $n = k + 1$ admit slightly different description allowing (sub)matrix transposition and were completely studied before: the case where $n = k$ is a classical linear preserver problem for the ordinary determinant and was solved by Frobenius; the complete characterisation for the case where $n = k + 1$ was obtained in the previous paper by the authors.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Guterman, Andrey Yurkov

item.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. II
item.description: arXiv:2512.13445v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is the second in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. In this part we solve the linear preserver problem for the Cullis' determinant defined on the spaces of matrices of size $n\times k$ with $k \ge 4,\; n \ge k + 2$ and $n + k$ is odd. In comparison with the case when $n + k$ is even, in this case linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant could be singular and are represented as a sum of two linear maps: first is two-sided matrix multiplication and second is any linear map whose image consists of matrices, all rows of which are equal.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Guterman, Andrey Yurkov

item.title: On identity Seidel switches
item.description: arXiv:2601.04530v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An identity Seidel switch of a graph is a vertex subset whose Seidel switch produces an isomorphic graph. We distinguish the elementary abelian group of switching operations from the family of identity switches of a fixed graph, which need not be a group. We obtain an edge-count condition for identity switches and deduce that every vertex-identity switch has degree half the number of remaining vertices. In particular, no graph of order at least two has every vertex as an identity switch. For a two-vertex switching set inducing an edge, we characterize the switches admitting an isomorphism that preserves the endpoint pair, in terms of automorphisms of the remaining induced subgraph. We establish modification results under this additional hypothesis and give explicit constructions of identity switches. Counterexamples show why edge-count conditions and unrestricted modification assertions do not suffice.
item.dc:creator: Severino V. Gervacio

item.title: A Dyadic Frequency Law for a Perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-Recursion
item.description: arXiv:2603.16111v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-recursion defined by $$Q(1)=Q(2)=1,\qquad Q(n)=Q(n-Q(n-1))+Q(n-Q(n-2))+(-1)^n \quad(n\ge3).$$ for $n\ge3$. Clo\^itre proved that the recursion is globally well-defined and encoded its odd- and even-indexed subsequences by binary arches and canonical plane forests. Let $F(s)=\#\{n\ge1:Q(n)=2s-1\}$, and let $\nu_2(j)$ denote the exponent of $2$ in $j$. For every integer $k\ge0$, we prove the multiset identity $$ \{F(s):2^k\le s<2^{k+1}\}=\{3+\nu_2(j):1\le j\le 2^k\}. $$ The proof expresses frequencies as sums of plateau lengths and folds reflected gap pairs to identify the excess frequencies $F(s)-3$ with the outdegrees of a canonical plane tree. For $k\ge2$, the maximum $k+3$ occurs at $s_k=\lceil 2^{k+2}/3\rceil$, and the second-largest frequency $k+2$ occurs at $s_k+1$. As a corollary, the sum with marks $z^{F(s)-3}$ and dyadic block weights $2^{-ku}$, multiplied by the Dirichlet eta function $\eta(u)$, has the Euler product of $\zeta(u)$ with its factor at $2$ replaced by $(1-z2^{-u})^{-1}$. Finally, we prove that the dyadic defect $Q(2n)-2Q(n)$ attains order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ in absolute value along a subsequence.
item.dc:creator: Marco Mantovanelli

item.title: The Pentagon Graph Operator
item.description: arXiv:2604.18984v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The pentagon graph $C_5(G)$ of a finite simple graph $G$ is the edge-intersection graph of its induced cycles of length five. We prove that the dodecahedral graph is mapped to the icosahedral graph $I$, which is a fixed point of the operator. Our principal result classifies every graph obtained by adjoining one vertex to $I$: it is eventually fixed if the added vertex belongs to no induced pentagon, and it is expanding otherwise. The proof shows that every new pentagon gives rise to a tadpole hat within at most two iterations. More generally, an induced icosahedral core with $h$ tadpole hats gives the lower bound $12+h2^k$ on the orders of the iterates. We also establish a replication principle and construct two vertex-disjoint induced copies of the Shrikhande graph in its pentagon graph, yielding the bound $16\cdot2^k$. The general vanishing--periodic--expanding trichotomy is included as background.
item.dc:creator: Severino V. Gervacio, Hiroshi Maehara, Phoebe Chloe F. Ramos

item.title: Structural Classes for Chollet's Permanent Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2604.24192v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1982, Chollet conjectured that $\operatorname{per}(A\circ B)\le \operatorname{per}(A)\operatorname{per}(B)$ for Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$, where $\circ$ denotes the Hadamard (entrywise) product. In this paper, we study natural structural classes for which the conjecture holds. We first show that a stronger inequality holds for a broad class of matrices with bipartite support. We then introduce a simple way of joining positive semidefinite matrices and give conditions under which Chollet's inequality is preserved under this operation. For graph Laplacians, this operation corresponds to vertex coalescence and gives larger structured graph families satisfying Chollet's inequality from simpler graph classes.
item.dc:creator: Priyanshu Pant, Ranveer Singh

item.title: Two Results on Outer-String Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.12253v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An \emph{outer-string representation} of a graph $G$ is an intersection representation of $G$ where vertices are represented by curves (strings) inside the unit disk and each curve has exactly one endpoint on the boundary of the unit disk (the anchor of the curve). Additionally, if each two curves are allowed to cross at most once, we call this an \emph{outer-$1$-string representation} of $G$. If we impose a cyclic ordering on the vertices of $G$ and require the cyclic order of the anchors to respect this cyclic order, such a representation is called a \emph{constrained outer-string representation}. In this paper, we present two results about graphs admitting outer-string representations. Firstly, we show that for a bipartite graph $G$ (and, more generally, for any $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free graph $G$) with a given cyclic order of vertices, we can decide in polynomial time whether $G$ admits a constrained outer-string representation. Our algorithm follows from a characterization by a single forbidden configuration, similar to that of Biedl et al. [GD 2024] for chordal graphs. Secondly, we answer an open question from the same authors and show that determining whether a given graph admits an outer-1-string representation is NP-hard. More generally, we show that it is NP-hard to determine if a given graph $G$ admits an outer-$k$-string representation for any fixed $k\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: Todor Anti\'c, V\'it Jel\'inek, Jan Kratochv\'il, Peter Stumpf

item.title: $\boldsymbol{2}$-Neighbor Bootstrap Percolation on Odd Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.03687v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on a graph $G$ is a vertex-activation process that begins with a set of initially active vertices. In each subsequent round, every inactive vertex having at least $r$ active neighbors becomes active. Denote by $m(G,r)$ the minimum number of initially active vertices required for the activation process to spread to all remaining vertices of $G$. In this article, we consider the odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{O}_k\) and the bipartite odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{B}_k\), and prove that $m(\mathbbmsl{O}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+3k+2)/4\rceil$ and $m(\mathbbmsl{B}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+2k+3)/2\rceil$. The first formula confirms the quadratic-growth conjecture proposed in 2021 by Grippo, Pastine, Torres, Valencia-Pabon, and Vera.
item.dc:creator: Ali Mohammadian, Sina Rezaie Zareie, Behruz Tayfeh-Rezaie

item.title: Proper edge coloring with rainbow diamonds
item.description: arXiv:2606.06831v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the B-coloring defined by Gy\'arf\'as and S\'ark\"ozy, we introduce a new edge coloring called \emph{D-coloring}. For a graph $G$, a D-coloring of $G$ is a proper edge coloring such that every diamond subgraph is rainbow. The \emph{D-chromatic index} of $G$, denoted by $\chi'_D(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a D-coloring of $G$. Denote by $\Delta$ the maximum degree of $G$. We propose a Brooks-type conjecture stating that $\chi'_D(G)\le \frac{1}{2}\Delta^2+\frac{1}{2}\Delta$ and verify this conjecture for $\Delta\le 5$. We also prove a general upper bound $\chi'_D(G)\le \frac{9}{16}\Delta^2+\frac{1}{2}\Delta$.
item.dc:creator: Runze Wang

item.title: Non-Isomorphic Optimal Cayley Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.10954v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present eighty-nine optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs that are non-isomorphic to previously known optimal Cayley graphs with the same degree and diameter. For each graph, we provide comprehensive data on its parameters and structural invariants. Comparison with known constructions reported by Marston Conder on the Combinatorics Wiki and in related works reveals significant differences in girth, algebraic connectivity, domination number, automorphism group structure, cycle distributions, distance-related properties, and other graph invariants. These findings show that optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs are frequently non-unique. The new examples enlarge the catalogue of known optimal graphs and provide benchmarks for investigations in degree-diameter problems, algebraic graph theory, and extremal graph theory. Since some of the graphs were identified through randomized search techniques, the collection is not exhaustive.
item.dc:creator: Francesc Comellas

item.title: Bipartite cuts in Ramsey-Tur\'an style
item.description: arXiv:2606.20397v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every $K_5$-free $n$-vertex graph with sublinear independence number can be made bipartite by removing at most $n^2(1/18+o(1))$ edges, where the constant $1/18$ is best possible. The proof method is related to extensions of Tur\'an Theorem in edge-weighted settings, and part of the proof uses flag algebra. Using a similar flag algebra formulation, AI proved that every $K_6$-free and $K_7$-free $n$-vertex graph with sublinear independence number can be made bipartite by removing at most $n^2(1/12+o(1))$ and $n^2(1/9+o(1))$ edges, respectively. These constants are best possible.
item.dc:creator: J\'ozsef Balogh, Ce Chen, Bernard Lidick\'y

item.title: The structure of FAC posets and the Aharoni--Korman conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2607.02500v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A poset $P$ is said to satisfy the finite antichain condition, or FAC for short, if it has no infinite antichain. Such posets exhibit rich and complex structure, and it was conjectured by Aharoni and Korman in 1992 that any FAC poset $P$ possesses a chain $C$ and a partition into antichains such that $C$ meets every antichain of the partition. While a counterexample to this conjecture was recently discovered, in this paper we prove that the conjecture does hold true for a broad class of countable posets. In particular, we prove that the Aharoni--Korman conjecture holds for countable FAC posets containing no saturated chain $D$ such that either $D$ or its reverse $D^*$ is of the form $\bigoplus_{x\in\omega} D_x$, where each $D_x$ is infinite and co-well-founded. The proof of this result rests on novel structural theory for countable FAC posets, which may be of independent interest. One result states that every countable FAC poset is either scattered (contains no copy of the rationals) or may be broken up into a dense collection of scattered posets which reflect the structure of the poset as a whole. This provides a general reduction from arbitrary countable FAC posets to the far more tractable scattered ones. We also develop an extension $H(P)$ of a poset $P$ which includes ``limit points'' of $P$ and allows for intricate arguments involving these points. Amongst other points, one way in which $H(P)$ differs from existing poset completions and extensions is that it is sensitive to the order-type of a chain. Finally, we highlight a number of intriguing problems in this area which remain open.
item.dc:creator: Lawrence Hollom

item.title: Shifted-Binomial Coordinates of Dilated Binomial Polynomials: Multinomial Decimation and Arithmetic Structure
item.description: arXiv:2607.12173v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For integers $m\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, let $d=m+r-1$ and consider the unique expansion \[ \binom{mn}{d}=\sum_{k=1}^{d+1}T_{m,r,k}\binom{n+k-1}{d}. \] By a standard multisection of a rational generating function, the coordinates are a residue-class subsequence of multinomial coefficients: \[ T_{m,r,k}=[x^{mk-1}](1+x+\cdots+x^{m-1})^{m+r}. \] From this representation we obtain the exact support, a counting interpretation by words by drops (Theorem~\ref{thm:drops}), a reflection criterion (the nonzero row is palindromic precisely when $r\equiv2\pmod m$), and log-concavity, hence unimodality, of the nonzero row. An integer-valued polynomial argument gives the universal divisor $m/\gcd(m,r-1)$ of each row, and a prime-adic computation of the fixed divisor of $\binom{mX}{d}$ gives the exact greatest common divisor of each row, a sharpness criterion, and a family of rows in which the universal divisor is arbitrarily far from sharp. We also obtain the row sum $m^{m+r-1}$, a Catalan-number specialization, and explicit coefficient arrays for $m=2,3,4,5$. The methods are finite differences, multisection of rational generating functions, and fixed divisors of integer-valued polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhai Doukali

item.title: A 21-Coloring of the Plane Without Monochromatic Unit-Area Rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2609.00583v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Erd\H{o}s and Graham asked whether every finite coloring of the plane must contain a monochromatic rectangle of any prescribed area. Kova\v{c} gave a negative answer by constructing a $25$-coloring with no monochromatic rectangle of area $1$. We reduce the number of colors to $21$ by replacing the square cells in his construction with regular hexagons.
item.dc:creator: Gary Hu, Yumo Liu

item.title: Bounded Ratios of Lorentzian Polynomials II: Quadratic Derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2609.07098v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bounded monomial ratios for Lorentzian polynomials. We prove that, in degree $d\geq2$ and $n$ variables, the bounded ratios from quadratic derivatives generate all bounded ratios for every $M$-convex support if and only if $n\leq3$, $d=2$, or $(n,d)=(4,3)$. For four-variable cubics, the proof uses a decomposition into $M$-concave functions. We construct explicit counterexamples with full support for four-variable quartics and five-variable cubics, then extend these two examples to all remaining pairs.
item.dc:creator: Dijia Chen, Bowen Gan, Ivy Liu, Zemeng Wang, Chengzhi Wu

item.title: The smallest square tileable by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2609.19536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Croft, Falconer and Guy (Unsolved Problems in Geometry, Problem C5) exhibit a tiling of the 27 x 27 square by eight pairwise incomparable integer rectangles and remark that it is not known whether 27 is the smallest side length of a square that can be tiled by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles, no restriction being placed on the number of tiles. Knuth has since stated, in a 2019 draft of a section of The Art of Computer Programming, that 27 is indeed the smallest. We give a complete, independently reproducible proof: for every integer n <= 26 and every k >= 2, the n x n square admits no tiling by k pairwise incomparable integer rectangles. The proof combines two structural reductions with an exhaustive search over the 167538 surviving candidate tile sets, carried out by two independently written programs. The same search shows that at least eight tiles are needed at n = 27 and that the tile set of Croft, Falconer and Guy is the only one that tiles this square; it does so in exactly two arrangements up to symmetry. We also give explicit eight-tile tilings of the n x n square for every n >= 27, and seven-tile tilings for every n >= 34. With the classical lower bounds (every tiling of a rectangle by two or more pairwise incomparable rectangles uses at least seven, and no square of integer side less than 34 can be tiled by seven pairwise incomparable integer rectangles), this determines the least number of tiles for every square: there is no tiling for n <= 26, eight tiles are needed for 27 <= n <= 33, and seven for n >= 34. The complete software, build instructions and output logs are included as ancillary files.
item.dc:creator: George M. Georgiou

item.title: Fractal Hyper-Trees I. Combinatorial foundations: definition, enumeration, invariants, morphisms and the algebra $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb H\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)$
item.description: arXiv:2609.19895v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fractal Hyper-Trees (FHTs) are hypergraphs organized in levels: each level consists of disjoint connected clutters, and every edge strictly contains each lower component that it meets. Connected clutters and Schr{\"o}der hierarchies are the two extreme cases. Every FHT decomposes uniquely into the children of its top component, which carry smaller FHTs, and a host, an arbitrary connected clutter on these children. This gives an exact recurrence by size and depth and a species equation; the counts begin 1, 1, 4, 23, 231, 16947, 490083358 and are exact through nine vertices. Four interior moves (fusion, fission, aggregation, explosion) connect the FHTs on a given vertex set; every FHT on at least two vertices descends to the star by moves at distance at most one from the root, and $\kappa-1$, with $\kappa$ the number of edges, is its distance to the star. For FHTs with automorphism group $S\_4$, twisting the real group algebra by the sign character gives $\mathbb{C}\oplus\mathbb{H}\oplus M\_3(\mathbb{C})$, the finite algebra of Connes' description of the Standard Model. Conversely this algebra determines the group up to isomorphism and the class of a real 2-cocycle. The axioms select neither the group nor the twist: with the twist fixed as the sign of the action on the vertices, the algebra occurs exactly when $\mathrm{Aut}\,F\cong S\_4$ and some automorphism is odd on the vertices, at every size $v\ge4$. Every finite group is the automorphism group of a flat FHT, and every faithful action on a finite connected simplicial complex is rigidified into a flat FHT with the same reduced integral homology. All computations are deposited and their kind (exhaustive, sampled, exact or numerical) is stated.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Jacques Salone (UA, INSP{\'E} Guadeloupe, CRREF, LIM)

item.title: Exact Ehrhart Series of Birkhoff Polytopes via Constant Terms and Finite-Field Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2609.25863v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Ehrhart series of the $n$th Birkhoff polytope is $\sum_{r\geq0}H_n(r)z^r$, where $H_n(r)$ counts nonnegative integer $n\times n$ matrices whose row and column sums all equal $r$. We present an exact method for computing this series using constant terms and finite fields. A root filter expresses $H_n(r)$ as a weighted sum of the values $h_r(M)^n$, where $h_r$ is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial and $M$ ranges over multisets of $m$th roots of unity with $m=r+1$. Constant-term cancellation reduces the evaluation of $h_r(M)$ to a sum over repeated elements $a$ of $M$. For a particular $a$ of multiplicity $\mu_a$, the computation uses a generalized Todd coefficient of degree $\mu_a-2$. Sums of $h_r(M)^n$ over selected multiplicity classes are handled using symmetric function techniques. Together with the remaining individual evaluations, this gives $O_n(m^{n-5}+m^4)$ field operations for each admissible prime and fixed $n\geq5$. An explicit bound and the Chinese remainder theorem recover the integer counts, and Ehrhart symmetry determines the full series. The same method applies to the World Cup problem, which counts the same matrices with diagonal entries required to be $0$. We prove correctness and compute complete Birkhoff series through order $14$ and World Cup series through order $13$. The Birkhoff series for orders $10$--$14$ and the World Cup series for orders $9$--$13$ are tabulated in the appendices.
item.dc:creator: Xinru Jiang, Guoce Xin, Chen Zhang, Yueming Zhong

item.title: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
item.description: arXiv:2609.30310v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A polyhex is a connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, joined edge to edge, where each cell has area one. Kurz conjectured an upper bound for the area of the convex hull of a polyhex, after the corresponding problem for squares was solved. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells has area at most one sixth of the ceiling of $n^2+14n/3$, and that for every n this value is attained by a path made of three straight runs of nearly equal length. This proves the conjecture of Kurz and improves his bound by 1/6 when n is divisible by 3. The proof bounds the hull of the cell centres and three of its widths with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The upper bound is formalised in the Lean 4 proof assistant with the Mathlib library. We also show that for every n the extremal polyhex is unique up to rotation, reflection and translation, which an exhaustive search had confirmed for at most 12 cells. The proof of uniqueness was generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz, and it is also formalised in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Pragyaan Gaur

item.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal matching covered graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.30978v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is {\em matching covered} if each of its edges lies in a perfect matching. A matching covered graph is {\em minimal} if the removal of any edge results in a graph that is no longer matching covered. Lov\'asz and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B 23 (1977) 127--138] proved by ear decompositions that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ edges, and this bound is sharp for all even $|V(G)|\ge6$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (4) (2026) 559--606] determined the extremal graphs achieving this upper bound. In this paper, we prove that every minimal matching covered nonbipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(5|V(G)|-10)/2$ edges. Moreover, we show that if $G$ is not bicritical, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-14)/2$ edges and if $G$ is 3-connected and has at least 14 vertices, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-26)/2$ edges. All three bounds are sharp, and all the corresponding extremal graphs are characterized.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoling He, Fuliang Lu, Heping Zhang

item.title: Spectral Erd\H{o}s--Gallai Theorems for the \(\mathcal A_\alpha\)-Tensor of the \(s\)-Clique Hypergraph
item.description: arXiv:2610.08605v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The generalized Erd\H{o}s--Gallai theorem determines the maximum number of $s$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no matching of $t$ edges. We study its spectral analogue for the $\mathcal A_\alpha$-tensor of the $s$-uniform clique hypergraph. For $n\geq2t-1$, $3\leq s\leq2t-1$, and $0\leq\alpha\leq1$, we determine the maximum $\alpha$-$s$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex graphs with no matching of $t$ edges, and characterize all extremal graphs. When $t<s\leq 2t-1$, the unique extremal graph up to isomorphism is a $(2t-1)$-clique with isolated vertices. When $3\leq s\leq t$, the extremal graphs are selected from this graph and the join of a $(t-1)$-clique with an independent set. We give the exact order at which the join becomes extremal and determine when both graphs attain the maximum.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoqi Liu, Haiying Shan

item.title: A Sharp Basis-Mass Inequality for Binary Matroids without a Fano Minor
item.description: arXiv:2610.14370v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be a binary matroid of rank $r$ with no $F_7$-minor, and let $B_M^\star$ denote the maximum of its basis-generating polynomial over nonnegative weights of total mass $r$. We prove the sharp inequality $B_M^\star\leq 2^r/(r+1)$, with equality holding if and only if the simplification of $M$ is isomorphic to $M(K_{r+1})$. Binary matroids with no $F_7$-minor also form the largest minor-closed class of matroids on which this inequality holds. For each fixed rank $r$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-element rank-$r$ matroid maximising the number of bases in this class is graphic.
item.dc:creator: Haozhou Zhang

item.title: The \(\mathcal A_\alpha\)-Spectral Tur\'an Problem for \(s\)-Clique Tensors of \(K_{r+1}\)-Free Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.34196v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For integers $3\leq s\leq r$ and $0<\alpha<1$, we study the maximum spectral radius of the convex combination of the degree and adjacency tensors of the $s$-clique hypergraph of an $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graph. For $n\geq r$, every extremal graph is complete $r$-partite. For all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly in $\alpha$, the only possible extremal graphs are $T_r(n)$ and $K_1\vee T_{r-1}(n-1)$. There is a unique parameter $\alpha_n$ at which both attain the maximum; the former is uniquely extremal below $\alpha_n$ and the latter above it. Writing $c=((r-1)/r)^{s-1}$, we show that $\alpha_n=c+(s-1)c/n+O_{r,s}(n^{-2})$. The limiting maximum after normalization by $n^{s-1}$ is $\binom{r-1}{s-1}\max\{r^{1-s},\alpha(r-1)^{1-s}\}$. A sharp row-quotient bound at $\alpha=c$ identifies the limiting part proportions; local comparisons then determine the exact integer part sizes.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoqi Liu, Haiying Shan

item.title: The maximum spectral radius of connected graphs with prescribed order and size
item.description: arXiv:2610.34905v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1986, Brualdi and Solheid asked which connected graph of prescribed order and size has maximum adjacency spectral radius. We complete the classification for every feasible pair of parameters. We prove that no graph outside the dense and star threshold families is extremal, including at ties, and settle the range $n\le e+1$, where the star candidate is not defined. The final comparison \emph{between} the dense and star candidates is supplied by Damnjanovi\'c's Propositions~4.1--4.2, not reproved here. We combine an exact Bellman recursion with dense-core domination, fractional complete-split bounds, and a virtual-star inequality. Three remaining comparison families (J), (K1), and (K2) are established analytically and by exact polynomial and Sturm certificates. The exact certificates are implemented in Python/SymPy and SageMath.
item.dc:creator: Dragan Stevanovi\'c

item.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.37167v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503--1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522--1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].
item.dc:creator: Yun-Ping Deng, Xuanlong Ma

item.title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
item.description: arXiv:2610.39599v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.
item.dc:creator: Michael A. Allen, Kenneth Edwards

item.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
item.description: arXiv:2611.05423v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta\ge750$ satisfies the Borodin--Kostochka inequality $\chi(G)\le\max\{\omega(G),\Delta-1\}$, conjectured for all $\Delta\ge9$. Reed (1999) established the inequality for $\Delta\ge10^{14}$, and Liu, Sun, Wang and Zeng (2026) lowered the threshold to $5.3\times10^6$. To extend a random partial colouring over large cliques, we find repeated colours using adaptively chosen vertex-disjoint stars and apply Hall's theorem to the available colour lists. We verify the required probability bounds by rational and interval arithmetic with directed rounding.
item.dc:creator: Lizhong Chen

item.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
item.description: arXiv:2611.07138v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $\Lambda$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $\Lambda$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.
item.dc:creator: Eric Kubischta

item.title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.19508v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang

item.title: Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.19668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we give exact counting formulas as functions of $|X|$ in terms of finite sums and generating functions. Such pairs correspond bijectively to actions on $X$ of the semigroup presented by two generators and the prescribed relation. The proofs use images, fibers, and the decomposition of functional digraphs into directed cycles with rooted trees attached. Several constructions apply beyond these sixteen identities: they give recurrences for homomorphisms between arbitrary prescribed functional digraphs and formulas for pairs satisfying $f^a=g^b$, where $a,b$ are fixed positive integers. We also derive an explicit inclusion-exclusion formula over subsets of $X$ for the number of endofunctions $g$ on $X$ satisfying $B=gAg$ for arbitrary prescribed endofunctions $A,B$ on $X$. This generalizes the enumeration of compositional square roots, recovered when $A$ is the identity map.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev

item.title: An improved bound on the strong chromatic index via local flag algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.22031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A strong edge coloring is an edge coloring where two edges receive different colors if they are incident or joined by a third edge. For a graph $G$, the strong chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $\chi'_s(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a strong edge coloring of $G$. In this paper, using a local flag algebra method, we prove that for every graph $G$ of sufficiently large maximum degree $\Delta$, $\chi'_s(G)\le 1.6388\Delta^2$, improving the bound $1.73\Delta^2$ due to Davey, Hurley, de Joannis de Verclos, Kang, and Volec.
item.dc:creator: Runze Wang

item.title: The Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture I: three-dimensional lattice polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.22337v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume bound for lattice polytopes with $k\ge3$ interior lattice points: the Euclidean volume of such a lattice polytope is at most $6(k+1)$, with equality if and only if the polytope is affinely unimodularly equivalent to $\operatorname{conv}(0,2e_1,3e_2,6(k+1)e_3)$. The inequality is strict when the minimum lattice width is at least three. Together with the known cases $k=1,2$, this completely resolves the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Jinlong Tang, Sihao Tao, Zihao Zhang

item.title: The isolation number of uniform hypertrees
item.description: arXiv:2611.24477v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An isolating set of a hypergraph $H$ is a vertex set whose closed neighbourhood intersects every edge of $H$. The isolation number $\iota(H)$ is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Let $T$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. We prove that if $T$ has order $n$ and at least two edges, then $\iota(T)\le\lfloor n/(2r-1)\rfloor$, where $r\ge3$. Moreover, the bound is attained for every admissible order. Furthermore, we characterize all hypertrees attaining it by a construction using six types of marked hypertrees of orders $2r-1$, $3r-2$ and $4r-3$. For connected graphs of order $n$ with at least two blocks, all of which are triangles, we obtain the sharp bound $\lfloor n/5\rfloor$ on the cycle isolation number and characterize the graphs attaining it.
item.dc:creator: Minhui Li, Shumin Zhang, Junhao Qu

item.title: Fourier Bases from Optimal Eigenfunctions of Paley Graphs of Square Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.25727v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Bart De Bruyn, Sergey Goryainov, Yilin Xie, Weihao Yan, Ferdinando Zullo

item.title: Local Statistics of Random Permutations from Free Products
item.description: arXiv:2203.12250v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be uniformly random permutations of orders $2$ and $3$, respectively, in $S_{N}$, and consider, say, the permutation $\alpha\beta\alpha\beta^{-1}$. How many fixed points does this random permutation have on average? The current paper studies questions of this kind and relates them to surprising topological and algebraic invariants of elements in free products of groups. Formally, let $\Gamma=G_{1}*\ldots*G_{k}$ be a free product of groups where each of $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ is either finite, finitely generated free, or an orientable hyperbolic surface group. For a fixed element $\gamma\in\Gamma$, a $\gamma$-random permutation in the symmetric group $S_{N}$ is the image of $\gamma$ through a uniformly random homomorphism $\Gamma\to S_{N}$. In this paper we study local statistics of $\gamma$-random permutations and their asymptotics as $N$ grows. We first consider $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$, the expected number of fixed points in a $\gamma$-random permutation in $S_{N}$. We show that unless $\gamma$ has finite order, the limit of $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ as $N\to\infty$ is an integer, and is equal to the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ such that $H\cong\mathbb{Z}$ or $H\cong C_{2}*C_{2}$. Equivalently, this is the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ and having (rational) Euler characteristic zero. We also prove there is an asymptotic expansion for $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ and determine the limit distribution of the number of fixed points as $N\to\infty$. These results are then generalized to all statistics of cycles of fixed lengths.
item.dc:creator: Doron Puder, Tomer Zimhoni

item.title: Efficient space reduction techniques by optimized majority rules for the Kemeny aggregation problem
item.description: arXiv:2506.15097v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Kemeny aggregation problem consists of computing the consensus rankings of an election with respect to the Kemeny-Young voting method. These consensus rankings satisfy various fundamental properties and are the geometric medians of the votes in the election under the Kendall tau distance, which counts the number of pairwise disagreements. The NP-hard Kemeny aggregation problem admits important applications in various domains such as operations research, computational social choice, machine learning, and biology but faces a severe bottleneck in practice. In 2020, Milosz and the second author presented an approach to reduce the search space of the problem by solving the relative order of pairs of elements in those consensus rankings. In this article, we prove an optimized and fully parallelizable extension of this approach. We achieve significantly more space reduction while the parallel design reduces the time complexity from ${O}(n^3)$ to essentially ${O}(n^2)$ with significant computational speedups in practice. We then show how the constraints built by our approach can be rigorously combined with other methods such as Integer Programming and Finest Condorcet Partitioning to achieve a highly efficient, robust, and scalable solution approach to the Kemeny aggregation problem. Our methods are applicable to the more general constrained Kemeny aggregation ranking problem with immutable input pairwise constraints. Experiments with benchmark against the commercial solver Gurobi are performed on real and synthetic data.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Kien Phung, Sylvie Hamel

item.title: On the $h$-polynomials of cyclotomic standard graded commutative algebras
item.description: arXiv:2511.07937v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We call a standard graded commutative $\Bbbk$-algebra \textit{cyclotomic} if its $h$-polynomial has all its roots on the unit circle in the complex plane. Complete intersections provide typical examples of cyclotomic algebras, since the $h$-polynomial of any standard graded complete intersection is a product of polynomials of the form $1 + t + \cdots + t^{m-1}$. We refer to such polynomials as being \textit{of type CI}. A natural question is whether there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra whose $h$-polynomial is not of type CI. In this paper, we give a partial answer to this question. We show that the $h$-polynomial $h_R(t)$ of a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ is of type CI whenever $h_R(1) \in \{1, 4, 6\}$ or $h_R(1)$ is prime. On the other hand, if $n$ is a composite integer with $n \geq 8$, then there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ whose $h$-polynomial $h_R(t)$ is not of type CI and satisfies $h_R(1) = n$.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Higashitani, Kenta Ueyama

item.title: Equivalent bounded confidence processes
item.description: arXiv:2512.18016v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the bounded confidence model the opinions of a set of agents evolve over discrete time steps. In each round an agent averages the opinion of all agents whose opinions are at most a certain threshold apart. Here we assume that the opinions of the agents are elements of the real line. The details of the dynamics are determined by the initial opinions of the agents, i.e. a starting configuration, and the mentioned threshold -- both admitting uncountably many possibilities. Recently it was conjectured that for each starting configuration the set of thresholds can be partitioned into a finite number of intervals such that the evolution of opinions does not depend on the precise value of the threshold within one of the intervals. So, we may say that, given a starting configuration of initial opinions, there is only a finite number of equivalence classes of bounded confidence processes (and an algorithm to compute them). Here we systematically study different notions of equivalence. Under our broadest notion of equivalence we can also get rid of the initial starting configuration and end up with a finite number of equivalent bounded confidence processes for each given (finite) number of agents. This allows to precisely study the occurring phenomena for small numbers of agents without the jeopardy of missing interesting cases by performing numerical experiments. We exemplarily study the freezing time, i.e. number of time steps needed until the process stabilizes, and the degree of fragmentation, i.e. the number of different opinions that survive once the process has reached its final state.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Kurz

item.title: Independence of homogeneous GKM manifolds and symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2602.07734v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G/H$ be a simply connected homogeneous space of maximal rank. Then the maximal torus $T$-action on $G/H$ equips it with a structure of a Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson (GKM) manifold. We call the $T$-action $j$-independent if any $i\leq j$ pairwise distinct isotropy weights at a fixed point are linearly independent. Using weighted graphs, we show that the maximal independence of $G/H$ is $2$, $3$ or $n=\dim T$, and that the cases of $3$ or $n=\dim T$ correspond to some symmetric spaces of rank $>2$ by using the Lie bracket structure at the tangent space at identity coset. We classify all $4$-independent homogeneous spaces by studying the $3$- and $4$-cycles in the matroid of the respective root subsystem complement using Borel-de Siebenthal and Cartan classification results. In the classical $G$ cases our case study of maximal independence relies on signed weighted graphs, following the classical methods of Zaslavsky and Harari. In the exceptional simply laced $G$ cases we either present a $3$-cycle, or prove that there is none by reducing them only to those having a form $x+y=z$ for positive roots $x,y,z$ and find an affine hyperplane containing the respective root complement. As a corollary, using the results of Ayzenberg and Masuda, the lower-degree reduced rational cohomology groups of the orbit space $T\backslash G/H$ vanish.
item.dc:creator: Shintaro Kuroki, Grigory Solomadin

item.title: GKM Theory for Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices in Lie Type D
item.description: arXiv:2602.08366v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the manifold $Q_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ of isospectral real skew-symmetric matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern determined by a graph $\Gamma$. The compact torus $T^n$ acts naturally on $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ by conjugation, and this action can be studied using GKM theory. We prove two results about this manifold and its GKM graph. The first theorem describes how the GKM graph of $Q_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ is obtained from the GKM graph of the corresponding manifold $M_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ of isospectral Hermitian matrices. The second theorem shows that equivariant formality of $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ implies equivariant formality of $M_{\Gamma,\lambda}$, whereas the converse fails.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Zhukov

item.title: Self-similar dendrites with finite boundary and P-sprouts
item.description: arXiv:2605.11833v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Each self-similar dendrite K with a finite self-similar boundary defines a finite acyclic edge-labeled bipartite graph G, called the sprout of K. The paper shows that the sprout G determines the combinatorial properties of the dendrite K and its topological structure.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Tetenov, Ivan Yudin, Dmitrii Drozdov

item.title: Group action-stabilizer graph of group actions of a group on a set
item.description: arXiv:2607.11161v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we introduce the group action-stabilizer graph $GAS(G)$ of a group $G$ on a set $X$. Its vertex set is the collection of all non-trivial group actions of $G$ on $X$, and two vertices $\phi$ and $\psi$ are adjacent if and only if the normal subgroups $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\phi$ and $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\psi$ of $G$ intersect non-trivially, where $G_x^\phi$ and $G_x^\psi$ are the stabilizers of $x$ with respect to the actions $\phi$ and $\psi$, respectively. We show that $GAS(G)$ is obtained from the intersection graph of those normal subgroups of $G$ that occur as kernels of actions on $X$ by replacing each vertex by a clique of twin vertices, and we characterize a special subgraph $gas(G)$ of $GAS(G)$ in which the vertex set contains the actions $\phi$ of $G$ on $X$ such that the kernels $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\phi$ are distinct. We determine the number of group actions within some specific groups and find certain conditions under which $GAS(G)$ is equal to $gas(G)$. We also show that, for a finite nilpotent group $G$ with at least two prime divisors, $gas(G)$ is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^3p_2$, and its complement is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^2p_2^2$.
item.dc:creator: Nepur Ranjan Hazarika, Kukil Kalpa Rajkhowa

item.title: A few remarks on the Baez-Duarte Criterion
item.description: arXiv:2607.12084v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study exponentially damped M\"obius approximants in $\mathscr H=L^2([1,\infty),dt/t^{-2})$. With \[ \gamma_n(t)=\left\lfloor\frac tn\right\rfloor -\frac{\lfloor t\rfloor}{n},\qquad f(u)(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)e^{-nu}\gamma_n(t),\] we compute the relevant scalar products, characterize the M\"obius coefficients as the unique coefficients giving pointwise convergence to the constant function, and prove $\langle1 \mid f(u)\rangle\to1$. Vasyunin's formula expresses $F(e^{-u})=\|f(u)\|_2^2$ as an arithmetic cotangent sum. In the final section we give a criterion that would help in the analysis of asymptotics of $F(x)$ as $x\uparrow 1$.

item.title: Equilibrium Numbers in Non-Square Bimatrix Games
item.description: arXiv:2609.24878v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bimatrix games may have an exponential number of mixed Nash equilibria if both dimensions of the game are allowed to grow. Bounds on their maximal number give structural insights that have been used to construct hard-to-solve games. We show new sharp or asymptotically sharp bounds on the (polynomial) number of equilibria for generic games where one dimension of the game is fixed and the number of strategies of the other player grows. These results go beyond the hitherto studied square games. Our methods employ combinatorial properties of polytopes, and recent obstructions that relate to the graph of those polytopes. For $n\ge5$, we construct $3\times n$ games that have all $2n+1$ vertices of the best-response polytope as equilibrium strategies, proved using a simple case of the 4-color theorem for planar graphs. Generic $4\times 5$ games are shown to have at most 17 equilibria, using computer calculations with existing datasets for all combinatorial types of the relevant polytopes. For $d\times n$ games, we construct games where all but a fraction of $O(1/n)$ of the maximum number of vertices are equilibrium strategies.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Ickstadt, Thorsten Theobald, Bernhard von Stengel

item.title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2609.29756v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How much information can a single neuron remember? How many memories can neural networks retrieve without creating false memories? These questions are related to a basic question: how many Boolean threshold functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(a_0+\langle a,x\rangle)$, $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, are there? In this paper, we show that the number $T_n$ of distinct Boolean threshold functions is \[ T_n=2\binom{2^n-1}{n}\bigl(1+O(n^{-99})\bigr). \] Equivalently, the capacity of a single threshold neuron is $n^2-\log_2(n!)+1+O(n^{-99})$ bits, improving the $O(n)$ error term in the result of Kahn--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi to $O(n^{-99})$. To prove this, we show that, for $1\le r\le n-1$, and $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ are chosen at random from $\{-1,1\}^n$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left\{ \langle v_1,\ldots,v_r\rangle\cap\{-1,1\}^n =\{\pm v_1,\ldots,\pm v_r\} \right\} =1-O(n^{-99}). \] In the context of the Kanter--Sompolinsky Hamiltonian for memory retrieval, this identifies $r=n-1$ as a sharp threshold, at which, for almost every collection of $r$ memories, the only ground states are these memories and their negatives, confirming a weaker form of the Kalai--Linial--Odlyzko conjecture. It also settles a recent open problem posed by M. Anthony on the specification number of Boolean threshold functions. In addition, we show that, for every $1\le r\le n-1$, \[ \mathbb P\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\text{ are linearly dependent}\} =2\binom r2\,2^{-n}+O\!\left(2^{-n}e^{-cn}\right), \] confirming a conjecture of Kahn--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi.
item.dc:creator: Xinyuan Xie

item.title: Avoiding Distances
item.description: arXiv:2610.24803v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a finite planar point set $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$, let $a_1<a_2< \cdots < a_s$ denote the $s \leq {n \choose 2}$ different (Euclidean) distances between points in $X$. The aim is to retain as many of the points as possible such that certain imposed inter-pair distances are avoided. For example, we show that: (A) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, an independent set of size $0.2293 n$ in the unit distance graph determined by $X$ can be found in $O(n^2)$ time. For any fixed $k \in \mathbf{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that for any set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, and set $D$ of size $k$, there exists a subset $X' \subseteq X$ of size $|X'| \geq c_k |X|$ in which no pair of points is at some distance in $D$ (we say that $X'$ avoids distances in $D$). Such a set can be found efficiently. (B) (i) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/2$ that avoids the maximum distance; this bound cannot be improved. (ii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $8n/47$ that avoids both the minimum and maximum distance; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $5n/16$ points can be retained with this property. (iii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/7$ whose diameter is at most half the original diameter; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $n/6$ points can be retained with this property. (C) (i) For any $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for \textsc{MIS} in the minimum distance graph of $n$ points in the plane can be found in $2^{O(1/\varepsilon)} n^{O(1)}$ time. (ii) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, a maximum independent set in the graph of diameters can be computed in $O(n \log{n})$ time. The techniques used to handle the planar case can be extended to $\mathbf{R}^d$ for any fixed dimension $d$.

item.title: A tight upper bound on non-overlapping codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.21913v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Non-overlapping codes (also known as cross bifix-free codes or strong comma-free codes) have now been studied for over 60 years as part of information theory, with regular new applications appearing and much recent interest. Let $X$ be a $q$-ary non-overlapping code of length $n$. The paper contains a self-contained proof that \[ |X|\leq \left(\frac{q-1}{qe} +O(n^{-1/4})\right)\frac{q^n}{n} \] as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $q$ fixed, where $e$ is the base of the natural logarithm. The constant $(q-1)/(qe)$ improves, by a factor of $(q-1)/q$, the best previously known bound due to Levenshtein (1970). Indeed, constructions of large non-overlapping codes show that this constant is best possible. The paper builds on work by Fimmel, Michel, Pirot, Sereni and Str\"ungmann (2019), and by Stanovnik, Mo\v skon and Mraz (2024).

item.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
item.description: arXiv:2611.27828v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.
